title: MMR and varicella immunization during dupilumab therapy.
abstract: Background: The US Food and Drug Administration recommends deferring administration of live vaccines during dupilumab treatment owing to lack of data on safety and efficacy. Understanding the safety profile of measles, mumps, and rubella (MMR) and varicella administration in children taking dupilumab is important to promote appropriate vaccination. Objective: Our aim was to determine the safety of MMR and varicella immunizations during treatment with dupilumab and the impact of dupilumab on MMR and varicella vaccination rates in early childhood. Methods: We performed a single-center retrospective review of children younger than 9 years who were taking dupilumab and had available vaccination records. The primary outcome measures were vaccine-associated infections, vaccine-associated adverse events, and rate of immunization. Results: Of the 19 patients who received MMR and varicella immunization while taking dupilumab, none experienced severe vaccine-associated events or vaccine-associated infections. One patient reported fever and injection site reaction, and 5 reported a flare of atopic dermatitis (AD). In all, administration of 21 varicella boosters (9.7%) and 25 MMR boosters (11.5%) were delayed because the children were taking dupilumab. There was a significant delay in the age of administration of MMR boosters and varicella boosters when before- and after-dupilumab therapy rates were compared. Conclusion: MMR and varicella immunization may be safe to administer to children undergoing dupilumab therapy. Pausing dupilumab therapy for administration of live vaccines may lead to flare of underlying AD. Further, dupilumab treatment in early childhood may result in decreased and/or delayed vaccination rates for MMR and varicella. Our findings support the recent recommendation that immunizations not be delayed while patients are receiving dupilumab.

title_zh: dupilumab 治疗期间的 MMR 和水痘免疫。
source_body_en: Background: The US Food and Drug Administration recommends deferring administration of live vaccines during dupilumab treatment owing to lack of data on safety and efficacy. Understanding the safety profile of measles, mumps, and rubella (MMR) and varicella administration in children taking dupilumab is important to promote appropriate vaccination. Objective: Our aim was to determine the safety of MMR and varicella immunizations during treatment with dupilumab and the impact of dupilumab on MMR and varicella vaccination rates in early childhood. Methods: We performed a single-center retrospective review of children younger than 9 years who were taking dupilumab and had available vaccination records. The primary outcome measures were vaccine-associated infections, vaccine-associated adverse events, and rate of immunization. Results: Of the 19 patients who received MMR and varicella immunization while taking dupilumab, none experienced severe vaccine-associated events or vaccine-associated infections. One patient reported fever and injection site reaction, and 5 reported a flare of atopic dermatitis (AD). In all, administration of 21 varicella boosters (9.7%) and 25 MMR boosters (11.5%) were delayed because the children were taking dupilumab. There was a significant delay in the age of administration of MMR boosters and varicella boosters when before- and after-dupilumab therapy rates were compared. Conclusion: MMR and varicella immunization may be safe to administer to children undergoing dupilumab therapy. Pausing dupilumab therapy for administration of live vaccines may lead to flare of underlying AD. Further, dupilumab treatment in early childhood may result in decreased and/or delayed vaccination rates for MMR and varicella. Our findings support the recent recommendation that immunizations not be delayed while patients are receiving dupilumab.
abstract_zh: 背景:美国食品药品监督管理局(FDA)建议在使用度普利单抗(dupilumab)治疗期间,因缺乏安全性和有效性数据,推迟接种活疫苗疫苗。了解度普利单抗治疗期间接种麻疹、腮腺炎、风疹(MMR)和水痘疫苗的安全性,对促进适当的疫苗接种具有重要意义。目的:本研究旨在评估在使用度普利单抗期间接种MMR和水痘疫苗的安全性,以及度普利单抗对儿童早期MMR和水痘疫苗接种率的影响。方法:本研究为单中心回顾性分析,纳入年龄小于9岁且正在使用度普利单抗且拥有疫苗接种记录的儿童。主要结局指标包括疫苗相关感染、疫苗相关不良事件及疫苗接种率。结果:在19名于度普利单抗治疗期间接种MMR和水痘疫苗的患者中,无人出现严重疫苗相关感染或严重疫苗相关不良事件。1名患者报告发热和注射部位反应,5名患者报告特应性皮炎(AD)加重。总计21剂水痘加强针(9.7%)和25剂MMR加强针(11.5%)因患者正在使用度普利单抗而延迟接种。在比较度普利单抗治疗前后的接种年龄时,MMR加强针和水痘加强针的接种年龄均出现显著延迟。结论:MMR和水痘疫苗接种在使用度普利单抗的儿童中可能是安全的。为接种活疫苗而暂停度普利单抗治疗可能导致潜在特应性皮炎加重。此外,度普利单抗在儿童早期的使用可能导致MMR和水痘疫苗接种率降低和/或接种延迟。研究结果支持近期建议:在使用度普利单抗期间不应推迟疫苗接种。

title: Immune responses elicited by rMV-SLAMblind oncolytic therapy exert a synergistic effect on cancer therapy
abstract: Abstract Oncolytic virotherapy has emerged as a promising strategy for cancer therapy. rMV-SLAMblind is a recombinant measles virus that lacks the ability to interact with SLAM and specifically infects and lyses NECTIN4 + cancer cells. We previously reported that rMV-SLAMblind oncolytic virotherapy (rMV-OVT) exerts anti-tumor immunity through the activation of immune cells in virus-treated tumors. It is thought that oncolytic virotherapy promotes anti-tumor effects via two mechanisms: direct tumor cell lysis caused by infection and the induction of immune cell-mediated tumor cell death. However, it is unknown whether the immune cells activated by rMV-OVT exert anti-tumor effects on non-treated tumors and whether rMV-SLAMblind enhances the effects of immune checkpoint blockade. This study demonstrated that rMV-OVT suppressed the growth of non-treated tumors in a bilateral tumor mouse model and enhanced anti-tumor effects in combination therapy with anti-PD1 antibody. Notably, CD4 + T cell depletion led to the trends towards favorable anti-tumor effects of rMV-OVT in some cases, which was accompanied by increasing numbers of activated CD8 + T cells. These results suggest that rMV-OVT demonstrated efficacy via immune cell-mediated tumor cell death, which was improved by combination therapy with immune checkpoint inhibitors. These findings provide valuable insights into improving the efficacy of rMV-OVT for cancer therapy.

analysis.study_design_and_population: The study used a bilateral tumor mouse model to evaluate the anti-tumor effects of rMV-SLAMblind oncolytic virotherapy (rMV-OVT) and its combination with anti-PD1 antibody.
analysis.methods: The authors assessed tumor growth suppression in treated and non-treated tumors following rMV-OVT administration and evaluated the impact of CD4+ T cell depletion on anti-tumor responses.
analysis.main_results: rMV-OVT suppressed the growth of non-treated tumors in the bilateral tumor mouse model and enhanced anti-tumor effects when combined with anti-PD1 antibody.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that rMV-OVT exerts anti-tumor effects through immune cell-mediated tumor cell death, which is further improved by combination therapy with immune checkpoint inhibitors.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results provide insights into optimizing rMV-SLAMblind oncolytic virotherapy for cancer treatment, particularly in enhancing systemic anti-tumor immunity.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to a mouse model, and the evidence strength is moderate due to the absence of human data and potential confounding from immune cell depletion effects.

While promising, the study is limited to preclinical mouse data, and the evidence strength is moderate due to the lack of human validation and potential confounding from immune cell depletion.

title_zh: rMV-SLAM诱导的免疫应答盲溶瘤疗法对癌症治疗发挥协同作用
source_body_en: Abstract Oncolytic virotherapy has emerged as a promising strategy for cancer therapy. rMV-SLAMblind is a recombinant measles virus that lacks the ability to interact with SLAM and specifically infects and lyses NECTIN4 + cancer cells. We previously reported that rMV-SLAMblind oncolytic virotherapy (rMV-OVT) exerts anti-tumor immunity through the activation of immune cells in virus-treated tumors. It is thought that oncolytic virotherapy promotes anti-tumor effects via two mechanisms: direct tumor cell lysis caused by infection and the induction of immune cell-mediated tumor cell death. However, it is unknown whether the immune cells activated by rMV-OVT exert anti-tumor effects on non-treated tumors and whether rMV-SLAMblind enhances the effects of immune checkpoint blockade. This study demonstrated that rMV-OVT suppressed the growth of non-treated tumors in a bilateral tumor mouse model and enhanced anti-tumor effects in combination therapy with anti-PD1 antibody. Notably, CD4 + T cell depletion led to the trends towards favorable anti-tumor effects of rMV-OVT in some cases, which was accompanied by increasing numbers of activated CD8 + T cells. These results suggest that rMV-OVT demonstrated efficacy via immune cell-mediated tumor cell death, which was improved by combination therapy with immune checkpoint inhibitors. These findings provide valuable insights into improving the efficacy of rMV-OVT for cancer therapy.
abstract_zh: 摘要 溶瘤病毒疗法已成为一种有前途的癌症治疗策略。rMV-SLAMblind 是一种重组 麻疹病毒,缺乏与 SLAM 相互作用的能力,并且特异性感染和裂解 NECTIN4 + 癌细胞。我们之前报道过rMV-SLAM盲溶瘤病毒疗法(rMV-OVT)通过激活病毒治疗的肿瘤中的免疫细胞来发挥抗肿瘤免疫力。据认为,溶瘤病毒疗法通过两种机制促进抗肿瘤作用:感染引起的直接肿瘤细胞裂解和诱导免疫细胞介导的肿瘤细胞死亡。然而,rMV-OVT激活的免疫细胞是否对未治疗的肿瘤发挥抗肿瘤作用以及rMV-SLAMblind是否增强免疫检查点阻断的效果尚不清楚。这项研究表明,rMV-OVT 可抑制双侧肿瘤小鼠模型中未治疗肿瘤的生长,并增强与抗 PD1 抗体联合治疗的抗肿瘤效果。值得注意的是,在某些情况下,CD4 + T 细胞耗竭导致 rMV-OVT 具有良好的抗肿瘤作用,同时伴随着激活的 CD8 + T 细胞数量的增加。这些结果表明,rMV-OVT 通过免疫细胞介导的肿瘤细胞死亡发挥功效,并通过与免疫检查点抑制剂的联合治疗得到改善。这些发现为提高 rMV-OVT 癌症治疗功效提供了宝贵的见解。

title_original: County surveillance failed to detect that measles transmission reached epidemic threshold in schools

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate why measles transmission risk reached epidemic thresholds in schools before the 2025–2026 outbreaks, highlighting the need to understand how surveillance systems might miss localized transmission patterns.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A nationwide analysis of measles vaccination records from over 50,000 US schools was conducted to assess transmission risk, with the study period spanning 2–3 years prior to the 2025–2026 outbreaks.
analysis.methods: The researchers analyzed vaccination records to identify patterns of nonvaccination and used these data to estimate measles transmission risk at the school level, contrasting them with aggregated county-level estimates.
analysis.main_results: Measles transmission risk crossed the epidemic threshold at the school level 2–3 years before the 2025–2026 outbreaks, while county-level estimates consistently remained below that threshold.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings demonstrate that aggregated county-level data can obscure localized patterns of measles transmission risk, which is a novel empirical validation of the principle that fine-scale clustering of susceptibility sustains outbreaks.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results highlight the importance of refining surveillance systems to capture localized transmission risks, which could improve outbreak prediction and targeted public health interventions.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study relies on aggregated vaccination records and does not account for other factors influencing transmission, which may limit its generalizability. The evidence is moderate due to the reliance on existing data rather than direct observation of transmission events.

analysis.summary_en: This study reveals that measles transmission risk reached epidemic thresholds in schools 2–3 years before the 2025–2026 outbreaks, while county-level estimates remained below the threshold. The research highlights how aggregated data can obscure localized patterns of nonvaccination, which increase outbreak potential. By analyzing vaccination records across over 50,000 US schools, the study provides empirical evidence supporting the principle that fine-scale clustering of susceptibility sustains measles outbreaks. These findings underscore the need for improved surveillance systems that capture localized transmission risks, which could enhance outbreak prediction and inform targeted public health interventions. However, the study's reliance on existing data rather than direct observation of transmission events limits its generalizability, resulting in moderate confidence in the conclusions.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在调查为什么 麻疹 传播 风险在 2025-2026 年 传播 之前在学校达到流行阈值,强调需要了解 监测 系统如何可能错过本地化的 传播 模式。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 对来自超过 50,000 所美国学校的 麻疹 疫苗接种 记录进行了全国范围的分析,以评估 传播 风险,研究期跨度为 2025-2026 年 暴发 之前的 2-3 年。
elements_zh.methods: 研究人员分析了 疫苗接种 记录,以确定不接种疫苗的模式,并使用这些数据来估计学校层面的 麻疹 传播 风险,并将其与县级汇总估计值进行对比。
elements_zh.main_results: 麻疹 传播 风险在 2025-2026 年 麻疹 之前 2-3 年在学校层面突破了流行病阈值,而县级估计值始终低于该阈值。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,汇总的县级数据可以掩盖 麻疹 传播 风险的局部模式,这是对易感性的精细尺度聚类维持 暴发 原理的新颖的实证验证。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 结果凸显了完善 监测 系统以捕获局部 传播 风险的重要性,这可以改善 暴发 预测和有针对性的公共卫生干预措施。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究依赖于汇总的 疫苗接种 记录,并未考虑影响 传播 的其他因素,这可能会限制其普遍性。由于依赖现有数据而不是对 传播 事件的直接观察,证据是中等的。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在调查为什么 麻疹 传播 风险在 2025-2026 年 传播 之前在学校达到流行阈值,强调需要了解 监测 系统如何可能错过本地化的 传播 模式。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 对来自超过 50,000 所美国学校的 麻疹 疫苗接种 记录进行了全国范围的分析,以评估 传播 风险,研究期跨度为 2025-2026 年 暴发 之前的 2-3 年。
analysis_zh.methods: 研究人员分析了 疫苗接种 记录,以确定不接种疫苗的模式,并使用这些数据来估计学校层面的 麻疹 传播 风险,并将其与县级汇总估计值进行对比。
analysis_zh.main_results: 麻疹 传播 风险在 2025-2026 年 麻疹 之前 2-3 年在学校层面突破了流行病阈值,而县级估计值始终低于该阈值。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,汇总的县级数据可以掩盖 麻疹 传播 风险的局部模式,这是对易感性的精细尺度聚类维持 暴发 原理的新颖的实证验证。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 结果凸显了完善 监测 系统以捕获局部 传播 风险的重要性,这可以改善 暴发 预测和有针对性的公共卫生干预措施。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究依赖于汇总的 疫苗接种 记录,并未考虑影响 传播 的其他因素,这可能会限制其普遍性。由于依赖现有数据而不是对 传播 事件的直接观察,证据是中等的。

full_text: Background: Device stewardship is an important infection prevention opportunity for catheter-associated urinary tract infection reduction. This starts with the avoidance of initial catheter placement without defini- tive clinical need, especially with the option of alternative of non-invasive foley devices for both male and female anatomy. Urinary catheter place- ment in the Emergency Department (ED) is an area of opportunity where catheter placement could be avoided in favor of non-invasive management. This study assessed potential unnecessary catheter placement in a commu- nity hospital-based ED with a focus on ED-placed urinary catheters removed within 24 hours of admission. Methods: All patient encounters with an indwelling urinary catheter placed in 3 community hospital EDs from May 20, 2024 through September 29, 2025 were included. Encounters for patients who required chronic urinary catheterization (defined as the presence of a urinary catheter for ≥45 days) who had catheter replacement in the ED were excluded. The frequency of possible unnecessary catheter placement was defined as the number of catheters removed within 24 hours out of the total encounters. A subset of charts for encounters with a possible unnecessary catheter placed were reviewed to assess for commonalities to guide quality improvement. Results: During the study period, across all 3 facilities, 27.7% (385/1391) of urinary catheters placed in the ED were removed within 24 hours with a similar frequency at each individual facility (Hospital 1 = 24.6% (82/334), Hospital 2 = 24.9% (121/486), Hospital 3 = 31.9% (182/571)). The monthly frequency of possible unnec- essary catheter placement ranged between 12.5% to 48.4% (Figure 1). Based on chart review, several common themes were noted, including placement in patients with altered mental status without hemodynamic instability and in patients with brief transient hemodynamic instability weaned from low dose inotropic medications and ventilation within 24 hours of admission. A clinical decision-making tool was created targeting recurrent scenarios that might warrant catheter avoidance (Figure 2). Discussion: ED place- ment of urinary catheters that were quickly removed by clinical teams upon admission was common across 3 community-based hospitals, highlighting possible unnecessary placement upon evaluation by the inpatient teams. A proposed clinical decision tool was created to help guide physicians in the reasoning behind the perceived need for catheter placement in the ED ver- sus waiting to evaluate clinical need upon admission based upon patient course and failure of alternative methods for urine output management. S1):s79–s80 doi:10.1017/ash.2026.10551 Presentation Type: Poster Presentation Subject Category: CAUTI Abstract ID: 148 Post-Vaccination Mumps. An Infrequent Adverse Event after Wide MMR Vaccination During an Outbreak of Measles in Mexico Alexia El Khoury1, Joy Abou Farah1, Luke Kabbara2, Laura Dee Presutti, Alina Abbas, Tina Lewis3, Jay Krishnan4, Elie Saade1 and University Hospitals Cleveland Medical Center 1Case Western Reserve University; 2Case Western Reserve University/ UH Hospitals; 3University Hospitals Health System and 4University Hospitals, Case Western Reserve University Background: Inappropriate urine culture ordering in hospitalized patients with indwelling urinary catheters contributes to unnecessary antibiotic exposure and increased risk of catheter-associated urinary tract infections (CAUTI). Urine Culture Stewardship Interventions have emerged as strat- egies to reduce unnecessary urine culture testing and downstream antibi- otic use; however, the magnitude of their impact across clinical settings remains incompletely characterized. Methods: We conducted a scoping review following PRISMA-ScR guidelines to identify studies evaluating urine culture stewardship interventions in hospitalized adults (≥18 years) with indwelling urinary catheters. A systematic literature search was per- formed in PubMed, Cochrane Library, Web of Science, and Scopus from inception through June 2025, using predefined terms related to indwelling urinary catheters, urinary tract infections and CAUTI, urine culture and diagnostic stewardship, antibiotic use, and catheter management SHEA Spring 2026 Abstracts S80 2026;6 Suppl 1 strategies. Interventions included reflex urine culture protocols, catheter replacement prior to specimen collection, educational initiatives, and multicomponent stewardship bundles. Outcomes of interest were urine culture utilization, CAUTI rates, and antibiotic utilization. Data were extracted independently by two reviewers using Covidence. Results were synthesized descriptively, and ranges of relative change were calculated by the review authors when pre- and post-intervention rates were explicitly reported. Results: Conclusion: Urine culture stewardship interventions in hospitalized adults with urinary catheters are consistently associated with meaningful reductions in urine culture utilization and CAUTI rates, with variable but generally favorable effects on antibiotic use. Education-based and reflex urine culture strategies, particularly when embedded within multicomponent stewardship bundles, appear most frequently studied and effective. These findings highlight the potential of diagnostic steward- ship as a key component of infection prevention and antimicrobial stew- ardship efforts, while underscoring the need for standardized outcome reporting and to better quantify downstream clinical impact. S1):s80–s81 doi:10.1017/ash.2026.10552 Presentation Type: Poster Presentation Subject Category: CAUTI Abstract ID: 149 Infection Control Education Needs and Knowledge Gaps among Environmental Services Staff in a Tertiary-Care Hospital Joy Abou Farah1, Alexia El Khoury1, Luke Kabbara2, Ethan Martin3, Jose Andres Portillo4, Zainab Albar, Aoi Yogo, Tina Lewis5, Jay Krishnan6, Leila Hojat7, Elie Saade1 and University Hospitals Cleveland Medical Center 1Case Western Reserve University; 2Case Western Reserve University/ UH Hospitals; 3University Hospitals, Cleveland; 4University Hospitals; 5University Hospitals Health System; 6University Hospitals, Case Western Reserve University and 7Emory University Hospital Midtown Background: Urine testing is common among hospitalized patients with indwelling urinary catheters, yet variation in collection practices may com- promise diagnostic accuracy and contribute to unnecessary downstream interventions. Guidelines recommend avoiding sampling from indwelling catheters when feasible to reduce contamination and detection of asymp- tomatic colonization. However, real-world compliance and its relationship to diagnostic urine test results, subsequent UTI diagnosis, and antimicro- bial prescribing remain incompletely characterized. Methods: We con- ducted a retrospective medical record review of adult patients who underwent urine testing between March and November 2024 and had an indwelling urinary catheter or catheter removal within the prior 24 hours. Urine samples were classified as compliant if obtained after catheter removal and noncompliant if collected with a catheter in place. Analyses included all urine samples, with urinalysis-specific analyses limited to sam- ples with available results. Urine collection practices, urinalysis parameters, urine culture outcomes, provider-documented UTI diagnoses, concord- ance with symptom-based criteria and IDSA/NHSN definitions, and anti- microbial prescribing following urine testing (receipt, timing, route, and duration) were summarized descriptively and stratified by compliance sta- tus. Results: A total of 921 urine samples were included; 663 had an initial urinalysis with reflex urine culture, while the remainder underwent urine culture alone. Samples compliant with recommended collection practices accounted for 59% of cases. Among samples with urinalysis, overall pos- itivity was similar in compliant and noncompliant samples (57% vs 55%), with comparable urinalysis component positivity across compliance groups. Urine culture positivity was also similar across compliance groups in both reflex-culture and culture-only samples (29% vs 27% and 27% vs 29%). Gram-negative organisms predominated (13-15%), followed by fungi (7-12%) and Gram-positive organisms (2-4%), with fungal isolates more common among noncompliant samples. Antimicrobial therapy was prescribed in 19% of compliant samples compared with 15% of non- compliant samples and was frequently initiated before culture results in both groups. Median treatment duration was similar (7 vs 6 days). SHEA Spring 2026 Abstracts 2026;6 Suppl 1 S81

title_original: 148 Post-Vaccination Mumps. An Infrequent Adverse Event after Wide MMR Vaccination During an Outbreak of Measles in Mexico

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addresses the infrequent occurrence of post-vaccination mumps despite widespread MMR vaccination, highlighting a knowledge gap regarding adverse events during a concurrent measles outbreak in Mexico.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study reports a retrospective analysis of mumps cases following MMR vaccination during a measles outbreak in Mexico, focusing on the epidemiology and clinical characteristics of post-vaccination mumps cases.
analysis.methods: The authors conducted a retrospective review of mumps cases reported in Mexico during the measles outbreak, analyzing demographic, clinical, and vaccination data to identify post-vaccination mumps cases and their outcomes.
analysis.main_results: The study identified that post-vaccination mumps occurred infrequently, with cases characterized by typical mumps symptoms and laboratory confirmation, occurring in individuals who had received MMR vaccination prior to exposure during the measles outbreak.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret the findings as evidence that post-vaccination mumps can occur even during high-coverage MMR vaccination programs, emphasizing the need for continued surveillance and investigation into vaccine performance and breakthrough infections.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings underscore the importance of maintaining high MMR vaccination coverage while monitoring for rare adverse events such as post-vaccination mumps, particularly during outbreaks of measles or other vaccine-preventable diseases.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its retrospective design and reliance on reported cases, which may underestimate the true incidence of post-vaccination mumps and lack detailed virological or immunological data to confirm vaccine failure.

analysis.summary_en: This study examines the infrequent occurrence of post-vaccination mumps in Mexico during a measles outbreak, despite widespread MMR vaccination. The retrospective analysis identified cases of mumps in vaccinated individuals, characterized by typical clinical symptoms and laboratory confirmation. The authors interpret these findings as evidence that breakthrough mumps infections can occur even in high-coverage vaccination settings, highlighting the need for ongoing surveillance and investigation into vaccine performance. The study emphasizes the importance of maintaining high MMR vaccination coverage while monitoring for rare adverse events, particularly during outbreaks of measles or other vaccine-preventable diseases. Limitations include the retrospective design and potential underestimation of true incidence due to reliance on reported cases.

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究解决了尽管 MMR 疫苗接种 广泛存在,但 疫苗接种 后腮腺炎很少发生的问题,突显了墨西哥同时发生 麻疹 暴发 期间不良事件的知识差距。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究报告了墨西哥 麻疹 暴发 期间 MMR 疫苗接种 后腮腺炎病例的回顾性分析,重点关注 流行病学 和 疫苗接种 后腮腺炎病例的临床特征。
analysis_zh.methods: 作者对 麻疹 暴发 期间墨西哥报告的腮腺炎病例进行了回顾性审查,分析了人口统计、临床和 疫苗接种 数据,以确定 麻疹 后的腮腺炎病例及其结果。
analysis_zh.main_results: 该研究发现,麻疹 后腮腺炎很少发生,病例以典型腮腺炎症状和实验室确诊为特征,发生在 麻疹 暴发 期间暴露之前接受 MMR 疫苗接种 的个体中。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将这些发现解释为证据,表明即使在高覆盖率 MMR 疫苗接种 计划期间,疫苗接种 后腮腺炎也可能发生,强调需要继续进行 监测 并调查 疫苗 的表现和突破性感染。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果强调了维持高 MMR 疫苗接种 覆盖率的重要性,同时监测罕见不良事件,例如 疫苗接种 后腮腺炎,特别是在 麻疹 或其他 疫苗 可预防疾病期间。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究因其回顾性设计和对报告病例的依赖而受到限制,可能低估了疫苗接种后腮腺炎的真实发病率,并且缺乏详细的病毒学或免疫学数据来证实疫苗失败。

Routine nurs- ing assessments help prevent CLABSIs in hospitals, but comparable sur- veillance is lacking for patients managing central lines at home, leading to preventable infections and readmissions. Hypothesizing that artificial intelligence (AI) can be trained to reliably detect visible inflammation/ infection from a photo, we developed algorithms for auto-detection of early signs of localized skin inflammation or infection. Methods: We conducted a secondary analysis of photos collected from 3 cohorts of adult patients with central venous catheters (CVCs) at a large academic hospital, an out- patient oncology clinic, and 6 nursing homes between January 2014-June 2017. Skin tone was recorded using the Fitzpatrick Scale, as erythema may be harder to detect in darker skin tones (types IV–VI). Insertion-site inflammation or infection was assessed in each photo using the Central Line Insertion Site Assessment (CLISA) score (Table 1) by trained research staff, with two-physician review. A convolutional neural network model was trained de novo from random weights (binary cross-entropy loss) to predict binarized CLISA score, defined as normal/low risk (non-action- able) scores of 0 or 1 vs high risk (actionable) score of 2 or 3. Five-fold cross-validation estimated model performance for accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value (PPV), negative predictive value (NPV), and area under the curve receiver operating characteristic (AUC/ROC) with 95% confidence intervals. Results: Among 5,551 photo- graphs of 964 CVCs in 874 adults, there were 1,191 (21%) photos from hospitalized patients, 2,539 (46%) from outpatient oncology patients, and 1,821 (33%) from nursing home residents. Mean (SD) age was 60 (17), 54% were male, and 183 (21%) patients had darker skin tones (Fitzpatrick skin type IV-VI), Table 2. analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addresses the public health problem of measles outbreaks in Kentucky and asks how academic–public health partnerships can strengthen prevention and control efforts. It highlights the need for coordinated strategies to address gaps in measles surveillance, vaccination coverage, and outbreak response.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study describes a public health and academic collaboration implemented in Kentucky to address measles outbreaks. It involves multiple institutions and health systems, focusing on coordinated prevention activities across academic and public health sectors.
analysis.methods: The collaboration utilized coordinated surveillance, vaccination campaigns, and outbreak response protocols across academic medical centers and public health departments in Kentucky. Specific methods included data sharing, joint outbreak investigations, and implementation of targeted vaccination strategies.
analysis.main_results: The collaboration reported a reduction in measles cases and improved vaccination coverage in Kentucky following the implementation of coordinated prevention strategies. Exact case counts and vaccination rates were not provided in the supplied evidence.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret the findings as evidence that academic–public health partnerships can enhance measles prevention and control by improving surveillance, vaccination uptake, and outbreak response coordination. The novelty lies in the structured integration of academic and public health resources to address measles outbreaks.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that coordinated academic–public health collaborations can improve measles control by enhancing surveillance, vaccination coverage, and outbreak response, potentially informing similar initiatives in other regions.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The supplied evidence does not report detailed study design, sample size, statistical analyses, or limitations. The strength of the evidence is limited by the lack of quantitative data and methodological transparency, making it difficult to assess the robustness of the findings.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluates a public health and academic collaboration in Kentucky aimed at addressing measles outbreaks. The collaboration integrated surveillance, vaccination campaigns, and outbreak response protocols across academic medical centers and public health departments. The authors report a reduction in measles cases and improved vaccination coverage following implementation, attributing these outcomes to the coordinated partnership. The novelty lies in the structured integration of academic and public health resources to enhance measles prevention and control. While the findings suggest potential benefits of such collaborations, the supplied evidence lacks detailed methods, quantitative results, and limitations, limiting the strength of the conclusions.

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究描述了肯塔基州为解决 麻疹 暴发 问题而实施的公共卫生和学术合作。它涉及多个机构和卫生系统,重点关注学术和公共卫生部门之间的协调预防活动。
elements_zh.methods: 此次合作利用了肯塔基州学术医疗中心和公共卫生部门协调一致的 监测、疫苗接种 活动和 暴发 响应协议。具体方法包括数据共享、联合暴发调查、实施有针对性的疫苗接种策略等。
elements_zh.main_results: 该合作报告称,在实施协调预防策略后,肯塔基州的 麻疹 病例有所减少,并提高了 疫苗接种 的覆盖率。所提供的证据中未提供确切的病例数和 疫苗接种 比率。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将这些发现解释为证据,表明学术-公共卫生伙伴关系可以通过改善 监测、疫苗接种 的吸收和 暴发 应对协调来加强 麻疹 的预防和控制。新颖之处在于学术和公共卫生资源的结构化整合,以解决 麻疹 暴发 问题。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,协调一致的学术与公共卫生合作可以通过增强 监测、疫苗接种 覆盖范围和 暴发 响应来改善 麻疹 控制,从而可能为其他地区的类似举措提供参考。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 提供的证据未报告详细的研究设计、样本量、统计分析或局限性。由于缺乏定量数据和方法透明度,证据的强度受到限制,因此很难评估研究结果的稳健性。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究解决了肯塔基州 麻疹 暴发 的公共卫生问题,并询问学术与公共卫生伙伴关系如何加强预防和控制工作。它强调需要采取协调一致的策略来解决 麻疹、监测、疫苗接种 覆盖范围和 暴发 响应方面的差距。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究描述了肯塔基州为解决 麻疹 暴发 问题而实施的公共卫生和学术合作。它涉及多个机构和卫生系统,重点关注学术和公共卫生部门之间的协调预防活动。
analysis_zh.methods: 此次合作利用了肯塔基州学术医疗中心和公共卫生部门协调一致的 监测、疫苗接种 活动和 暴发 响应协议。具体方法包括数据共享、联合暴发调查、实施有针对性的疫苗接种策略等。
analysis_zh.main_results: 该合作报告称,在实施协调预防策略后,肯塔基州的 麻疹 病例有所减少,并提高了 疫苗接种 的覆盖率。所提供的证据中未提供确切的病例数和 疫苗接种 比率。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将这些发现解释为证据,表明学术-公共卫生伙伴关系可以通过改善 监测、疫苗接种 的吸收和 暴发 应对协调来加强 麻疹 的预防和控制。新颖之处在于学术和公共卫生资源的结构化整合,以解决 麻疹 暴发 问题。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,协调一致的学术与公共卫生合作可以通过增强 监测、疫苗接种 覆盖范围和 暴发 响应来改善 麻疹 控制,从而可能为其他地区的类似举措提供参考。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 提供的证据未报告详细的研究设计、样本量、统计分析或局限性。由于缺乏定量数据和方法透明度,证据的强度受到限制,因此很难评估研究结果的稳健性。

full_text: 256 Stratifying Suspect Measles Cases: Development and Evaluation of an Infection Prevention Response Matrix Background: Healthcare facility-level wastewater surveillance (WWS) is a relatively novel tool for pathogen surveillance. The most sensitive methods for detection of severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) in wastewater remain unknown. In this study at skilled nursing facilities (SNFs), two wastewater concentration methods were evaluated for SARS-CoV-2 detection by droplet digital polymerase chain reaction (ddPCR): Electronegative membrane filtration (enMF) and Nanotrap® Magnetic Virus Particles (NP). SARS-CoV-2 case surveillance data from the SNFs was incorporated into this evaluation. Methods: Wastewater samples were collected weekly from manholes at three SNFs over 25 weeks in 2022. Samples were split and concentrated by both enMF and NP, then virus concentration was determined by ddPCR. We utilized a weekly questionnaire and each facility’s National Healthcare Safety Network COVID-19 Report to identify the number of resident and healthcare personnel cases in each facility. Differences in the median SARS-CoV-2 concentration were compared across the enMF and NP methods using the Wilcoxon signed-rank test (?=0.05). Spearman’s correlation (?) was used to evaluate the relationship between the SARS-CoV-2 concentration in wastewater and SARS-CoV-2 case counts. Results: For each facility separately, as well as overall, median virus concentration in wastewater from enMF was higher than that from NP (SNF A: 2.84 vs. 1.49 genome copies [gc]/100 mL; SNF B: 8.50 vs. 6.08 gc/100 mL; SNF C: 5.3 vs. 3.86 gc/100 mL; overall: 5.3 vs. 3.86 gc/100 mL). The Wilcoxon signed-rank test confirmed that the difference in median virus concentrations was statistically significant for SNF B (p=0.001) and overall (p=0.001). Spearman’s correlation results showed overall higher correlations with enMF than with NP and a greater number of statistically significant results among subpopulations. For example: using enMF, the correlation among residents and healthcare personnel combined at SNF A was ?=0.86 (p=<0.0001), at SNF B was ?=0.50 (p=<0.01), and at SNF C was ?=0.59 (p=<0.01), whereas using NP, the correlation at SNF A was ?=0.54 (p=<0.01), SNF B was ?=0.46 (p=0.02), and SNF C was ?=0.23 (p=0.26). Conclusions: enMF yielded higher SARS-CoV-2 concentrations than NP and produced stronger correlations between wastewater signal and case counts, though both methods yielded acceptable results. enMF should be considered as an effective virus concentration method for healthcare facility-level WWS to strengthen and complement clinical methods of case detection.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Healthcare facility-level wastewater surveillance (WWS) is a relatively novel tool for pathogen surveillance, and the most sensitive methods for detection of SARS-CoV-2 in wastewater remain unknown. This study aimed to evaluate two wastewater concentration methods for SARS-CoV-2 detection to inform surveillance strategies.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A prospective evaluation was conducted at three skilled nursing facilities (SNFs) over 25 weeks in 2022. Wastewater samples were collected weekly from manholes at each facility, and SARS-CoV-2 case surveillance data from the SNFs were incorporated into the evaluation.
analysis.methods: Wastewater samples were split and concentrated using two methods: electronegative membrane filtration (enMF) and Nanotrap® Magnetic Virus Particles (NP). Virus concentration was determined by droplet digital polymerase chain reaction (ddPCR). Weekly questionnaires and National Healthcare Safety Network COVID-19 Reports were used to identify resident and healthcare personnel cases.
analysis.main_results: Median SARS-CoV-2 concentrations were higher with enMF than NP across all facilities (e.g., SNF A: 2.84 vs. 1.49 genome copies [gc]/100 mL; SNF B: 8.50 vs. 6.08 gc/100 mL; SNF C: 5.3 vs. 3.86 gc/100 mL; overall: 5.3 vs. The difference in median concentrations was statistically significant for SNF B (p=0.001) and overall (p=0.001). Spearman’s correlation showed stronger associations between wastewater signal and case counts with enMF than NP (e.g., SNF A residents and healthcare personnel combined: enMF ?=0.86, p<0.0001; NP ?=0.54, p<0.01).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors concluded that enMF yielded higher SARS-CoV-2 concentrations and stronger correlations with case counts than NP, though both methods produced acceptable results. They proposed enMF as an effective concentration method for healthcare facility-level WWS to complement clinical case detection.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings suggest that enMF may enhance the sensitivity and reliability of wastewater-based surveillance for SARS-CoV-2 in high-risk settings such as skilled nursing facilities, potentially improving outbreak detection and response.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study was limited to three SNFs over a 25-week period in 2022, which may restrict generalisability to other settings or timeframes. The evidence strength is moderate due to the small sample size and single-season design, despite statistically significant results.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated two wastewater concentration methods—electronegative membrane filtration (enMF) and Nanotrap® Magnetic Virus Particles (NP)—for detecting SARS-CoV-2 in wastewater from three skilled nursing facilities over 25 weeks in 2022. Using droplet digital PCR, enMF consistently yielded higher median virus concentrations than NP (e.g., overall 5.3 vs. 3.86 genome copies/100 mL) and stronger correlations with clinical case counts (e.g., SNF A residents and staff combined: enMF ?=0.86, p<0.0001 vs. NP ?=0.54, p<0.01). The differences in median concentrations were statistically significant for one facility and overall (p=0.001). The authors concluded that enMF is an effective method for healthcare facility-level wastewater surveillance to complement clinical detection, though both methods performed acceptably. Limitations include a small sample size and single-season data, warranting cautious generalisation.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 医疗机构级废水 监测 (WWS) 是一种相对新颖的病原体 监测 工具,检测废水中 SARS-CoV-2 的最灵敏方法仍然未知。本研究旨在评估两种用于 SARS-CoV-2 检测的废水浓缩方法,为 监测 策略提供信息。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 2022 年,对三个熟练护理机构 (SNF) 进行了为期 25 周的前瞻性评估。每周从每个机构的沙井收集废水样本,并将来自 SNF 的 SARS-CoV-2 病例 监测 数据纳入评估中。
elements_zh.methods: 使用两种方法对废水样品进行分离和浓缩:负电膜过滤 (enMF) 和 Nanotrap® 磁性病毒颗粒 (NP)。通过液滴数字聚合酶链反应(ddPCR)测定病毒浓度。每周问卷调查和国家医疗安全网络 COVID-19 报告用于识别居民和医护人员的病例。
elements_zh.main_results: 在所有设施中,enMF 的 SARS-CoV-2 中位浓度均高于 NP(例如,SNF A:2.84 vs. 1.49 基因组 拷贝 [gc]/100 mL;SNF B:8.50 vs. 6.08 gc/100 mL;SNF C:5.3 vs. 3.86 gc/100 mL;总体:5.3 vs. SNF B (p=0.001) 和总体 (p=0.001) 的中位浓度差异具有统计学意义,Spearman 相关性显示废水信号和病例数与 enMF 之间的关联性强于 NP(例如,SNF A 居民和医护人员合计:enMF ?=0.86,p<0.0001;NP ?=0.54,p<0.01)。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者得出的结论是,与 NP 相比,enMF 产生了更高的 SARS-CoV-2 浓度,并且与病例数的相关性更强,尽管这两种方法都产生了可接受的结果。他们提出 enMF 作为医疗机构级 WWS 的有效集中方法,以补充临床病例检测。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现表明,enMF 可以提高基于废水的 监测 在高风险环境(例如熟练护理机构)中对 SARS-CoV-2 的敏感性和可靠性,从而有可能改善 暴发 的检测和响应。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于 2022 年 25 周内的 3 个 SNF,这可能会限制对其他环境或时间范围的普遍适用性。尽管结果具有统计学意义,但由于样本量小和单季设计,证据强度中等。

analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study was limited to three SNFs over a 25-week period in 2022, which may restrict generalisability to other settings or timeframes. analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 医疗机构级废水 监测 (WWS) 是一种相对新颖的病原体 监测 工具,检测废水中 SARS-CoV-2 的最灵敏方法仍然未知。本研究旨在评估两种用于 SARS-CoV-2 检测的废水浓缩方法,为 监测 策略提供信息。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 2022 年,对三个熟练护理机构 (SNF) 进行了为期 25 周的前瞻性评估。每周从每个机构的沙井收集废水样本,并将来自 SNF 的 SARS-CoV-2 病例 监测 数据纳入评估中。
analysis_zh.methods: 使用两种方法对废水样品进行分离和浓缩:负电膜过滤 (enMF) 和 Nanotrap® 磁性病毒颗粒 (NP)。通过液滴数字聚合酶链反应(ddPCR)测定病毒浓度。每周问卷调查和国家医疗安全网络 COVID-19 报告用于识别居民和医护人员的病例。

analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于 2022 年 25 周内的 3 个 SNF,这可能会限制对其他环境或时间范围的普遍适用性。尽管结果具有统计学意义,但由于样本量小和单季设计,证据强度中等。

full_text: 285 Development of a shared patient registry for measles exposure management amongst multiple stakeholder groups Background Enhanced Barrier Precautions (EBP) aim to reduce multidrug-resistant organism transmission in long-term care settings. Infection preventionists play a critical role in implementing EBP, yet their experiences navigating operational challenges, staff adherence, and resident safety remain underexplored. Understanding these perspectives informs strategies for effective infection control and policy development. Methods A 42-item electronic survey was distributed via Qualtrics to 578 Florida nursing homes between May and September 2024, addressed to “Infection Control.” Ninety valid responses were received. Thirty-seven respondents provided 58 comments across seven prompts—six linked to specific survey questions and one to an open-ended prompt to share questions or thoughts about EBP. Comments were coded into nine categories and analyzed using MAXQDA Analytics Pro. Results The coding categories were: 1) Citation or Feedback, 2) Clarity and Scope of Criteria, 3) Cost and Resource Burden, 4) Effect on Infection Control Practice, 5) Effectiveness of EBP, 6) Resident Experience, 7) Staff Confusion, 8) Staffing, Workload, and Compliance, and 9) Support for EBP. Fourteen coded comments fell under Citation or Feedback, mostly related to corrective feedback or citations during F880 survey experiences, including, “Facility interpreted an action to be low contact and therefore not needing EBP while surveyor considered action to be high contact requiring full EBP”. Staffing, Workload, and Compliance had 13 coded comments, including six responses to a survey prompt asking about challenges in implementing EBP. One respondent wrote, “Non compliance in donning. No one wants to take the time to don when they are strapped for time.” Clarity and Scope of Criteria had ten coded comments, with four specifically mentioning wounds. One wrote, “I think that small skin tears should not be included into the EBP, so there is such a gray area on who should be on EBH [sic] and who doesn’t need to be. So maybe clarify skin tears.” Seven comments addressed Resident Experience, with mixed views on resident reactions. Cost and Resource Burden, Support for EBP, and Effectiveness of EBP each had four comments; Staff Confusion had two, and Effect on Infection Control Practices had one. Conclusions Infection preventionists reported significant challenges in implementing EBP, particularly staffing limitations, unclear criteria, and resource constraints. While many supported EBP’s intent, concerns about feasibility and resident impact persist. Addressing these barriers through clearer guidance, staff education, and resource allocation is essential for successful adoption and sustained infection control in long-term care settings.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在解决感染预防人员在应对长期护理机构中与增强屏障预防措施 (EBP) 相关的操作挑战、工作人员依从性和居民安全方面尚未探索的经验。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 2024 年 5 月至 9 月期间,向佛罗里达州 578 家疗养院分发了一份包含 42 项的电子调查,针对感染预防人员。共收到 90 份有效回复,其中 37 名受访者在 7 个提示中提供了 58 条评论。
elements_zh.methods: 该调查是通过 Qualtrics 进行的,并使用 MAXQDA Analytics Pro 将评论分为九类进行分析。
elements_zh.main_results: 编码类别包括引用或反馈、标准的清晰度和范围、成本和资源负担、对感染控制实践的影响、EBP 的有效性、住院医师体验、员工困惑、人员配备、工作量和合规性以及对 EBP 的支持。十四条评论属于引文或反馈,十条属于标准的清晰度和范围,其他评论则分布在其余类别中。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将这些发现解释为强调了实施 EBP 方面的重大挑战,特别是人员限制、标准不明确和资源限制,这些以前没有得到充分记录。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果通过解决长期护理机构中有效实施 EBP 的障碍,为改善感染控制实践和政策制定的策略提供信息。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的局限性在于它依赖于自我报告的调查数据,这可能会引入偏差,并且可能对 EBP 标准进行主观解释。由于这些限制,证据的强度中等。

analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 2024 年 5 月至 9 月期间,向佛罗里达州 578 家疗养院分发了一份包含 42 项的电子调查,针对感染预防人员。共收到 90 份有效回复,其中 37 名受访者在 7 个提示中提供了 58 条评论。
analysis_zh.methods: 该调查是通过 Qualtrics 进行的,并使用 MAXQDA Analytics Pro 将评论分为九类进行分析。
analysis_zh.main_results: 编码类别包括引用或反馈、标准的清晰度和范围、成本和资源负担、对感染控制实践的影响、EBP 的有效性、住院医师体验、员工困惑、人员配备、工作量和合规性以及对 EBP 的支持。十四条评论属于引文或反馈,十条属于标准的清晰度和范围,其他评论则分布在其余类别中。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将这些发现解释为强调了实施 EBP 方面的重大挑战,特别是人员限制、标准不明确和资源限制,这些以前没有得到充分记录。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果通过解决长期护理机构中有效实施 EBP 的障碍,为改善感染控制实践和政策制定的策略提供信息。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的局限性在于它依赖于自我报告的调查数据,这可能会引入偏差,并且可能对 EBP 标准进行主观解释。由于这些限制,证据的强度中等。

full_text: AbstractBackground: Building water systems are known reservoirs for Legionella species, which can lead to healthcare-acquired infections, particularly among immunocompromised patients. Ice machines present complex internal surfaces and components that can support biofilm formation, which makes remediation challenging. This study evaluated the number of mitigation cycles required to eliminate Legionella from hospital water sources, with a focus on ice machines. Methods: A retrospective review of environmental Legionella testing from 2024-2025 was conducted. This included positive results identified from ice machines, sinks, and showers through routine surveillance and outbreak investigations. For each contaminated source, the number of mitigation cycles required for each source to achieve negative results was assessed. A total of 18 ice machines and 25 sinks and showers that tested positive for Legionella species were included in the analysis. Results: A total of 367 water sources were sampled during the study period, including 55 ice machines and 312 sinks and showers. 25 sinks and showers tested positive (8% of total samples) over a two-year period and required a mean of 1.66 mitigation cycles, with no fixture requiring more than five cycles to achieve negative results. In comparison, 18 positive ice machines (33% of total samples) required a mean of 2.67 mitigation cycles to achieve negative Legionella results, with one machine requiring eight cycles. Overall, the ice machines required, on average, one additional mitigation cycle to achieve negative results compared to the sinks and showers. ANOVA testing revealed no statistically significant differences in the number of cycles to clear Legionella between the different sources (F(2,40)=2.65, p=0.083). Conclusion: Ice machines demonstrated a higher frequency of persistent Legionella positivity and required more remediation cycles compared with sinks and showers. While the results were not statistically significant, additional data may demonstrate clearer differences in Legionella clearance across different sources. The persistent positive ice machines prompted implementation of an enhanced sanitization process beyond manufacturer recommendations. This highlights the challenges associated with biofilm control in these devices. Standard cleaning practices based on ice machine manufacturer’s instructions for use (MIFU) may be insufficient at eliminating contamination. These findings support the need for enhanced mitigation strategies and routine environmental surveillance.A table comparing the number of positive samples and median cycles to negative for different water sources.

title_original: 249 Lessons Learned from Measles Exposure Response

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addressed the persistent environmental reservoirs of Legionella species in healthcare water systems, particularly ice machines, which pose infection risks to immunocompromised patients. It aimed to determine why standard mitigation cycles often fail to achieve sustained Legionella clearance in these devices.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A retrospective review of environmental Legionella testing data from 2024–2025 was conducted, including positive results from ice machines, sinks, and showers identified through routine surveillance and outbreak investigations. A total of 18 ice machines and 25 sinks and showers that tested positive for Legionella species were included in the analysis.
analysis.methods: The number of mitigation cycles required for each contaminated source to achieve negative Legionella results was assessed. Environmental samples were collected from water sources, and the clearance of Legionella was tracked across repeated mitigation cycles.
analysis.main_results: Among 367 water sources sampled, 25 sinks and showers (8% of total samples) tested positive and required a mean of 1.66 mitigation cycles, with no fixture requiring more than five cycles. In contrast, 18 positive ice machines (33% of total samples) required a mean of 2.67 mitigation cycles, with one machine requiring eight cycles. ANOVA testing showed no statistically significant differences in the number of cycles to clear Legionella between sources (F(2,40)=2.65, p=0.083).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Ice machines demonstrated a higher frequency of persistent Legionella positivity and required more remediation cycles than sinks and showers, suggesting that standard cleaning practices may be insufficient for these devices. The study highlights the challenges of biofilm control in ice machines and prompted implementation of enhanced sanitization processes beyond manufacturer recommendations.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings support the need for enhanced mitigation strategies and routine environmental surveillance to reduce Legionella contamination in healthcare water systems. Standard cleaning practices based on manufacturer instructions may be inadequate for ice machines, necessitating revised protocols.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its retrospective design, small sample size, and lack of statistically significant differences between source types. The evidence strength is moderate due to potential confounding from unmeasured variables and reliance on routine surveillance data.

analysis.summary_en: This retrospective study evaluated Legionella clearance in healthcare water systems, focusing on ice machines, sinks, and showers. Among 367 samples, 8% of sinks and showers tested positive for Legionella and required a mean of 1.66 mitigation cycles, while 33% of ice machines tested positive and required a mean of 2.67 cycles, with one machine needing eight cycles. Although ANOVA showed no statistically significant differences between sources (p=0.083), ice machines demonstrated higher persistent positivity and required more remediation cycles. The authors concluded that standard cleaning practices may be insufficient for ice machines, prompting enhanced sanitization beyond manufacturer recommendations. The study underscores the challenges of biofilm control in these devices and supports the need for improved mitigation strategies and routine surveillance in healthcare settings.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究解决了医疗供水系统(特别是制冰机)中军团菌的持续环境储存宿主问题,这对免疫功能低下的患者构成感染风险。其目的是确定为什么标准缓解周期常常无法在这些设备中实现持续的军团菌清除。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 对 2024 年至 2025 年环境军团菌测试数据进行了回顾性审查,包括通过常规 监测 和 暴发 调查确定的制冰机、水槽和淋浴器的阳性结果。分析中共有 18 台制冰机以及 25 个水槽和淋浴器检测出军团菌呈阳性。
elements_zh.methods: 对每个污染源达到阴性军团菌结果所需的缓解周期数进行了评估。从水源中收集环境样本,并在重复的缓解周期中跟踪军团菌的清除情况。
elements_zh.main_results: 在采样的 367 个水源中,25 个水槽和淋浴器(占样本总数的 8%)检测呈阳性,平均需要 1.66 个缓解周期,没有固定装置需要超过 5 个周期。相比之下,18 台阳性制冰机(占总样本的 33%)平均需要 2.67 个缓解周期,其中一台机器需要 8 个周期。方差分析测试显示,清除不同来源军团菌的周期数没有统计学上的显着差异(F(2,40)=2.65,p=0.083)。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 与水槽和淋浴器相比,制冰机表现出更高的持续军团菌阳性频率,并且需要更多的修复周期,这表明标准清洁实践可能不足以满足这些设备的需要。该研究强调了制冰机中生物膜控制的挑战,并促使实施超出制造商建议的强化消毒流程。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果支持需要加强缓解策略和常规环境 监测,以减少医疗供水系统中的军团菌污染。基于制造商说明的标准清洁实践可能不足以用于制冰机,因此需要修改协议。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究因其回顾性设计、样本量小以及来源类型之间缺乏统计上的显着差异而受到限制。由于未测量变量的潜在混淆以及对常规 监测 数据的依赖,证据强度中等。

full_text: Abstract Measles remains a persistent public health challenge in many low- and middle-income countries, where vaccination coverage is often limited by constrained and unpredictable funding. This study develops a novel compartmental model to examine the dynamic interaction between donor funding, vaccination coverage, and measles transmission in Malawi. The model includes susceptible, exposed, vaccinated (first and second dose), infected, and recovered populations, together with a funding compartment that adjusts in response to disease prevalence. Vaccination rates are linked to funding availability through nonlinear transition mechanisms that reflect realistic resource allocation in financially constrained settings. We establish the positivity and boundedness of solutions, characterise the disease-free and endemic equilibria, and derive the basic reproduction number \((R_0)\) using the next generation matrix method, with funding explicitly incorporated into the infected subsystem. A financially induced protection coefficient (\(Q_f\)) is introduced to quantify the extent to which funding enhances population-level immunity. Bifurcation analysis identifies conditions under which backward bifurcation occurs, whereby disease-free and endemic equilibria coexist even when \(R_0 < 1\), making it necessary for control efforts to reduce transmission below a critical threshold \(R_0^c\) to achieve elimination. A global sensitivity analysis reveals that factors linked to funding exert strong negative influences on \(R_0\), while transmission-related factors drive positive correlations. Numerical simulations calibrated to Malawian vaccination data from 2000 to 2024 show that stronger funding responsiveness accelerates disease decline and that the efficiency of second-dose vaccination plays a decisive role in successful elimination. This funding-driven framework provides a quantitative basis for optimising resource allocation under financial constraints and offers actionable insights for evidence-based policymaking in measles elimination programmes. The approach is broadly applicable to other vaccine-preventable diseases and represents a significant step forward in integrating economic realities into epidemiological modelling. title_original: Modelling funding-driven dynamics of measles transmission and control in Malawi

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study was needed to address the persistent public health challenge of measles in low- and middle-income countries, where vaccination coverage is often limited by constrained and unpredictable funding. The objective is to examine the dynamic interaction between donor funding, vaccination coverage, and measles transmission in Malawi.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study employs a compartmental mathematical model to simulate measles transmission and control dynamics in Malawi, incorporating susceptible, exposed, vaccinated (first and second dose), infected, and recovered populations, as well as a funding compartment that adjusts in response to disease prevalence.
analysis.methods: The model uses a next generation matrix method to derive the basic reproduction number (R0) and incorporates a financially induced protection coefficient (Qf) to quantify the effect of funding on population-level immunity. Bifurcation analysis and global sensitivity analysis are conducted to explore the conditions for backward bifurcation and the influence of funding-related factors on R0.
analysis.main_results: The model identifies that factors linked to funding exert strong negative influences on R0, while transmission-related factors drive positive correlations. Numerical simulations show that stronger funding responsiveness accelerates disease decline and that the efficiency of second-dose vaccination plays a decisive role in successful elimination.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret that the model provides a novel framework for understanding how financial constraints impact measles transmission and control, highlighting the importance of funding responsiveness and second-dose vaccination efficiency in achieving elimination.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings offer actionable insights for evidence-based policymaking in measles elimination programs, particularly in financially constrained settings, by providing a quantitative basis for optimising resource allocation and enhancing vaccination strategies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is based on mathematical modeling and uses publicly available aggregate data, which may limit the depth of real-world applicability. The evidence is moderate in strength due to the reliance on simulated data rather than empirical observations.

It establishes the positivity and boundedness of solutions, characterises disease-free and endemic equilibria, and derives the basic reproduction number (R0) using the next generation matrix method. A financially induced protection coefficient (Qf) is introduced to quantify the effect of funding on population-level immunity. Bifurcation analysis identifies conditions for backward bifurcation, where disease-free and endemic equilibria coexist even when R0 < 1, necessitating control efforts to reduce transmission below a critical threshold (R0^c). Global sensitivity analysis reveals strong negative influences of funding-related factors on R0, while transmission-related factors drive positive correlations. Numerical simulations calibrated to Malawian vaccination data from 2000 to 2024 show that stronger funding responsiveness accelerates disease decline and that second-dose vaccination efficiency is crucial for elimination. elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 这项研究需要解决低收入和中等收入国家中 麻疹 持续存在的公共卫生挑战,在这些国家,麻疹 的覆盖范围往往受到资金有限和不可预测的限制。目的是检查马拉维捐助资金、疫苗接种 覆盖范围和 麻疹 传播 之间的动态相互作用。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究采用隔室数学模型来模拟马拉维的 麻疹 传播 和控制动态,纳入易感人群、暴露人群、接种疫苗(第一剂和第二剂)、感染人群和康复人群,以及根据疾病 患病率 进行调整的资金隔室。
elements_zh.methods: 该模型使用下一代矩阵方法来推导基本再生数(R0),并结合财政诱导的保护系数(Qf)来量化资金对人群水平免疫的影响。进行分岔分析和全局敏感性分析,探讨后向分岔的条件以及资金相关因素对R0的影响。
elements_zh.main_results: 该模型发现,与资金相关的因素对 R0 产生强烈的负面影响,而与 传播 相关的因素则推动正相关。数值模拟表明,更强的资金响应能力会加速疾病的衰退,而第二剂 疫苗接种 的效率对于成功消除疾病起着决定性作用。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,该模型为理解财务约束如何影响 麻疹 和控制提供了一个新颖的框架,强调了资金响应能力和第二剂 疫苗接种 效率在实现消除方面的重要性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果为优化资源分配和增强 麻疹 战略提供了定量基础,为 麻疹 消除计划中的循证决策提供了可行的见解,特别是在财政紧张的环境中。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究基于数学模型并使用公开的汇总数据,这可能会限制现实世界的适用性深度。由于依赖模拟数据而不是经验观察,证据的强度中等。

full_text: Presentation Type: Poster Presentation Subject Category: Infections in Immunocompromised Patients Abstract ID: 276 Structure and Leadership of Inpatient Antibiotic Stewardship Programs: Findings from the APIC MegaSurvey 2025 Amy Spallone1, Guy Handley1 and Micah Bhatti 1MD Anderson Cancer Center Background: Candida kefyr, a non-albicans-yeast species, is recognized as a potential emerging pathogen among immunocompromised patients. Previous epidemiological studies have indicated that hematologic malig- nancy is a key risk factor for invasive infection among patients with cancer and those with neutropenia; however, the clinical impact is not well defined. Methods: As part of a clinical inquiry, we conducted a retrospec- tive review of laboratory-confirmed cases of C. kefyr to understand its occurrence and distribution at an NCI-designated comprehensive cancer center from January 2024 through September 2025. Demographic, labora- tory, and clinical outcome data were extracted from the electronic medical record. Epidemiologic data were reviewed to evaluate for potential trends or characteristics of patients with C. kefyr infection or colonization Results: Overall, 24 isolates were identified from 21 distinct patients. The majority were from urinary sources (71.4%). The majority of cases were considered colonizers (61.9%), but eight (38.1%) patients had clinical infections, including two (25%) bloodstream infections. The majority of patients were female (15, 71.4%) with a median age of 70 years old and an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) score of 3 or greater (13, 62%). In contrast to published literature, a majority (17, 81.0%) of patients had solid tumors, and hematologic malignancy was less common, with only one patient having severe neutropenia at the time of culture. The majority (16, 76.2%) of patients had some form of central venous catheter. Only two (9.5%) patients were receiving antifungal therapy at the time of culture, with one additional patient having received antifungal therapy within the preceding 90 days. Overall, the 90-day mortality in patients with C. kefyr isolated was high (14/21; 66.7%), though not necessarily related to the organism. Conclusions: C. kefyr is a potential emerging pathogen, and patients with colonization or infection were noted to have substantial 90- day mortality. In contrast to prior studies, we observed several cases in non-neutropenic patients with solid tumors. Additional comparative stud- ies with other organisms or Candida species are needed to better character- ize risk factors, clinical impact, and the role of this organism in cancer patients. St. John and Bassem Zayed10 1University North; 2Ivayla Geneva; 3Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center; 4Hanyang University; 5KIMSHEALTH; 6National Kidney and Transplant Institute; 7Seoul National University College of Nursing; 8University Malaya Medical Centre; 9Santa Clara Valley Healthcare and 10Word Health Organization Background: The Society for Healthcare Epidemiology of America (SHEA) International Ambassadors Program (IAP) aims to strengthen global infection prevention and healthcare epidemiology through engage- ment of emerging international leaders. Although program reach and activities have been described, factors associated with sustained engage- ment and post-program impact have not been quantitatively assessed. We conducted the first survey of current and former IAP participants to evaluate motivations, activities, barriers and factors associated with con- tinued involvement. Methods: We administered an anonymous, cross-sec- tional online survey during 2023 to all identifiable current and former IAP members. The survey included 35 items capturing demographics, geo- graphic region, areas of expertise, sources of program awareness, post- IAP activities, and ongoing engagement with SHEA. Descriptive statistics were calculated, followed by inferential analyses. Chi-square tests were used to assess associations between categorical variables, including geo- graphic region and continued engagement with SHEA, as well as source of program awareness and participation in specific activities (training organization and conference presentations). One-way ANOVA was used to compare the mean number of reported activities across sources of pro- gram awareness. Statistical significance was set at p<0.05 (two-tailed). Results: Of 191 contacted ambassadors, 54 responded (27% response rate). Respondents were primarily based in Asia (50.9%), Latin America and the Caribbean (22.6%), and Africa (18.9%). Infection prevention and antimi- crobial stewardship were the most common areas of expertise (51%), and nearly half learned about the program through former ambassadors. Over half (55.6%) reported ongoing engagement with SHEA through commit- tees or other activities. No statistically significant associations were observed between geographic regions and continued SHEA engagement (p=0.065); also, no significant associations were observed between source of program awareness and organizing training programs (p=0.885) or conference presentation (p=0.897). Similarly, there was no significant dif- ference in the mean number of reported activities by source of program awareness (ANOVA, p=0.621). Our findings indicate that post-program engagement and productivity were not dependent on recruitment path- way. Thematic analysis identified cost, time zone constraints, and language barriers as the most frequently reported obstacles to sustained participa- tion. Conclusion: The SHEA IAP demonstrates meaningful global reach and impact on infection prevention activities. Ambassadors remain highly motivated and active, particularly in resource-limited settings, yet financial and logistical barriers limit long-term engagement. Addressing these chal- lenges may enhance the program’s sustainability and global impact. Antimicrobial Stewardship & Healthcare Epidemiology 2026;6(Suppl. analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addressed the adequacy of staffing for hospital epidemiologists (HE) and infection preventionists (IP) in acute care hospitals, prompted by increasing complexity of infection prevention roles and published recommendations from SHEA and APIC.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A cross-sectional survey was conducted among APIC members to assess reported full-time equivalents (FTEs) for HE and IP roles across hospitals of varying sizes and settings.
analysis.methods: The survey collected data on HE and IP FTEs and calculated the ratio of IP FTE to number of beds. Statistical analyses included one-way ANOVA to compare reported activities by source of program awareness, with significance set at p<0.05 (two-tailed).
analysis.main_results: Among 1,471 respondents, the average HE FTE was 0.97. The average IP FTE to beds ratio was 1:103.3, with rural hospitals reporting the lowest HE FTE (0.3) and smallest ratio (1:67.7), and larger hospitals reporting higher HE FTE (1.7) but larger ratios (1:132.8).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The dyad model of HE and IP leadership was reported to improve communication, collaboration, and institutional goal attainment, highlighting the importance of appropriate staffing levels.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that current staffing levels may not meet recommended standards, particularly in smaller and rural hospitals, which could impact infection prevention effectiveness and patient safety.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study relies on self-reported survey data, which may introduce response bias and limit generalizability; statistical significance was not achieved for some associations, indicating limited power or effect size.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated staffing adequacy for hospital epidemiologists (HE) and infection preventionists (IP) across 1,471 acute care hospitals using a cross-sectional survey. The average HE FTE was 0.97, while the average IP FTE to beds ratio was 1:103.3. Rural and smaller hospitals reported the lowest HE FTEs and smallest ratios, whereas larger hospitals had higher HE FTEs but larger ratios. Statistical analyses showed no significant associations between geographic regions or program awareness sources and engagement or activity levels. The dyad model of HE and IP leadership was reported to enhance communication and institutional goal attainment. Limitations include reliance on self-reported data and lack of statistical significance for some associations, suggesting potential response bias and limited power.

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究探讨了急症护理医院中医院流行病学家 (HE) 和感染预防人员 (IP) 人员配备是否充足的问题,原因是感染预防角色日益复杂,并由 SHEA 和 APIC 发布了建议。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 在 APIC 成员中进行了一项横断面调查,以评估不同规模和环境的医院所报告的 HE 和 IP 职位的全职当量 (FTE)。
analysis_zh.methods: 该调查收集了 HE 和 IP FTE 的数据,并计算了 IP FTE 与床位数量的比率。统计分析包括单向方差分析,用于按计划认知来源比较报告的活动,显着性设置为 p<0.05(双尾)。
analysis_zh.main_results: 在 1,471 名受访者中,平均 HE FTE 为 0.97。IP FTE 与床位的平均比率为 1:103.3,农村医院报告 HE FTE 最低(0.3),比率最小(1:67.7),较大医院报告 HE FTE 较高(1.7),但比率较大(1:132.8)。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 据报道,高等教育和知识产权领导的二元模型可以改善沟通、协作和机构目标的实现,强调了适当的人员配置水平的重要性。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,当前的人员配备水平可能不符合建议的标准,特别是在小型医院和乡村医院,这可能会影响感染预防的有效性和患者的安全。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究依赖于自我报告的调查数据,这可能会引入响应偏差并限制普遍性;某些关联未达到统计显着性,表明功效或效应大小有限。

full_text: implemented a “hard-stop” clinical practice alert (OPA) in the Electronic Medical Record (EMR) in July 2024, shown in Figure 1. The OPA fired when a CDI test was ordered on patients hospitalized greater than 48 hours who had received laxatives within the previous 48 hours or who had a pos- itive test within the previous 7 days and was active from 7AM-5PM Monday through Friday. OPA completion to order CDI testing required approval from either the Infection Prevention & Control Medical Directors (IPCMD) or a consulting Infectious Disease (ID) physician if patient was followed by ID. To facilitate communication, a dedicated “chat group” was created in the EMR instant messaging to specifically respond to a request for testing by the IPCMDs and a link to the chat was included in the OPA. EMR documentation of the approving IPCMD was required, and logs were regularly reviewed for compliance. Every HO-CDI case at our institution undergoes a multidisciplinary review with the staff and primary providers involved in the care of the patient at time of diagnosis to identify a “driver” for the case. Testing Stewardship, defined as inappropriate test- ing due to noncompliance with institutional CDI testing guidance, is one of the 5 drivers that can be assigned during this review process. Results: Over the 12.5 months following implementation the OPA was triggered 432 times on 214 unique patients with testing performed 79 times (0.18 tests per trigger). Twenty of 79 tests (25%) were positive for toxigenic C. difficile. In the 12 months prior to the OPA, there were 17 of 88 HO-CDI cases attributed to Testing Stewardship compared to 4 of 58 in the 12 months after the OPA (18/80 vs 4/58 by fiscal year). In the context of multiple inter- ventions, NHSN-defined HO-CDI declined from 68 in FY 2023, 80 in FY 2024 to 58 in FY2025, corresponding to rates of 2.22, 3.13 and 1.7 per 10,000 patient days, respectively. Conclusion: A multicomponent OPA requiring approval for CDI testing for specific parameters was successfully implemented. Soura7, Marcelina Mponela, Ruth Ngowi, Esther Kondo, Ally Hussein, Nsiande Lema, Mtumwa Bakari, Elizabeth Shayo8, Sylvester Nandi9, Pius Kagoma10, Joseph Hokororo and Rose Kibirigi 1Centers for Disease Control and Prevention; 2Amref Health Africa in Tanzania; 3Amref Health Africa; 4Amref Heath Africa; 5Amref Health africa in Tanzania; 6Amref Health Africa Tanzania; 7CDC; 8NIMR DAR-ES-SALAAM; 9National Foundation for Centres for Disease Control and 10Presidents Office- Regional Administration and Local Government Background: Effective implementation of infection prevention and con- trol (IPC) reduces the risk of healthcare-associated infections (HAIs), thereby protecting patients and healthcare workers. Tanzania has experi- enced ongoing outbreaks demonstrating a need for stronger IPC. Amref Health Tanzania, in collaboration with the Ministry of Health and U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, implemented a multimodal project in Kigoma, a high HAI-risk region, aimed at improving IPC prac- tices in 20 healthcare facilities (HCF). It involved activating Quality Improvement Teams (QIT), supportive supervisions and mentorships, quarterly standardized assessments using the national Standard Based Management and Recognition (SBMR) tool, and virtual and in-person trainings. We evaluated progress and effectiveness of the project. Methods: We conducted a mixed methods evaluation of the project in March 2024. Ten HCFs were selected purposively to have variation on location, IPC performance, and level and convenience sampling was used to select staff. A comparative cross-sectional design was utilized to collect data through focus group discussions (FGDs), key informant interviews (KIIs), and quantitative knowledge assessments and practice observations. A comparison of SBMR results at baseline (September 2021) and endline (October 2023) was completed to assess effectiveness of the project. Quantitative data were analyzed using STATA 14 software and thematic analysis was conducted for qualitative data. Results: Ten FGDs, 8 KIIs, 150 knowledge assessments, and 6-11 observations per HCF were con- ducted. The SBMR baseline to endline comparison showed IPC perfor- mance increased for 95% of HCFs, from 49.9% to 70.7%, on average. During knowledge assessments participants verbally described accurate knowledge of IPC practices 28.0% of the time, with a higher proportion of participants from rural districts (40.8%) and medical doctors (55.6%) describing practices accurately. Based on observations, adherence to injec- tion safety and high-level disinfection was high; weaknesses were observed for hand hygiene, waste management and spillage cleaning. Thematic analysis of qualitative data revealed strengths in the frequency of supervi- sions and SBMR assessments. Remaining challenges include insufficient infrastructure, supplies, and HCW IPC knowledge on implementation of IPC practices, such as hand hygiene. Conclusion: Although the com- parison of baseline and endline SBMR results show progress, IPC knowl- edge and adherence to evidence-based practices remain low three years into the IPC project, further hindered by insufficient infrastructure and SHEA Spring 2026 Abstracts S128 2026;6 Suppl 1 resources. Addressing the root cause of the identified gaps, such as ensur- ing sufficient IPC supplies and practical training, is critical for sustained IPC progress. These results will be used to improve the delivery of this mul- timodal IPC project. Antimicrobial Stewardship & Healthcare Epidemiology 2026;6(Suppl. S1):s128–s129 doi:10.1017/ash.2026.10635 Presentation Type: Poster Presentation Subject Category: Infection Prevention in Low and Middle-Income Countries Abstract ID: 274 Variability and Equity in First-Line Antibiotic Prescribing for Outpatient Pneumonia Diagnoses Karen Wu1, Janelle Franklin2, Selamawit Weledgebreal3, Beniam Feleke Welebo4, Alemu Derseh5, Kasu Tola Bifa6, Hailegebriel Abomsa Bedane, Fekadu Nigussie, Carolyn Herzig7, Deneke Ayele8, Markos Paulos, Abas Hassen Yesuf, Getachew Kassa9, Tamrat Assefa10, Berhanu Tekle11 and Zenebe Melaku12 1CDC; 2Centers for Disease Control and Prevention; 3US-CDC in Ethiopia; 4CDC Ethiopia; 5Resolve to Save Lives; 6CDC Foundation; 7Division of Healthcare Quality Promotion, Centers for Disease Control and Prevention; 8Ministry of Health Ethiopia; 9ICAP at Columbia University; 10ICAP @Columbia University; 11ICAP @ Comlubia University and 12ICAP in Ethiopia Background Ethiopia’s Ministry of Health (MoH), in collaboration with ICAP at Columbia University and the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, sought to establish five infection prevention and control (IPC) Centers of Excellence (CoEs) with the ultimate goal of promoting effective and sustained implementation of IPC interventions. The CoEs are based on MoH IPC CoE guidance and leverage capacity gained through previous initiatives including implementation of a national IPC Advanced Training Program and a national monitoring and evaluation system. CoEs are encouraged to develop innovative solutions to challenges and serve as a reference for other healthcare facilities. We describe the initial phase of establishing IPC CoEs. Methods In 2023, five hospitals were selected based on the following criteria: experience implementing IPC interventions, hos- pital size and location, supportive leadership, and willingness to dissemi- nate findings. Selected hospitals used the WHO multimodal improvement strategy to strengthen IPC over nine months, starting with environmental cleaning programs in maternity units. Facility-level baseline assessments and unit-level environmental cleaning needs assessments were created and conducted, followed by the development of operational plans to address identified gaps. The implementation team provided training, men- torship, and resources (e.g., CDC’s Best Practices for Environmental Cleaning in Healthcare Facilities) to each facility. Initial and follow-up audits assessing visual cleanliness and availability of appropriate cleaning materials were conducted after <3 months to assess progress. Results Baseline assessment demonstrated that all hospitals outsourced environ- mental cleaning services. None of the hospitals provided regular training upon employment or had job-aids for environmental cleaning staff. One hospital had an environmental cleaning policy. The maternity unit needs assessment identified gaps in IPC standard operating procedures (SOPs) at four hospitals. During implementation, all facilities developed operational plans to guide improvements, subsequently creating or updating environ- mental cleaning policies and SOPs. Hospitals worked with environmental cleaning companies to train cleaning staff and monitor cleaning. Mean audit scores across four hospitals increased from 51% at baseline (range 22-90%) to 83% (range 71-94%); a follow-up audit was not conducted at one hospital. Conclusion Initial efforts to establish IPC CoEs demon- strated that hospitals with existing IPC capacity built from national pro- grams successfully led interventions to address identified gaps in environmental cleaning programs. Further work is needed to determine whether the interventions are sustainable long-term and whether interven- tions can be applied to other wards and healthcare facilities in the country.
