S1):s129 doi:10.1017/ash.2026.10636 Presentation Type: Poster Presentation Subject Category: Infections in Immunocompromised Patients Abstract ID: 275 Effect of a Diagnostic Order Set on Sexually-Transmitted Infection Co- Testing Lior Cohen Yatziv1, Scott Borgetti2, Alfredo Mena Lora3, Christine Zaky1 and Gabriela Mendez Gonzalez3 1University of Illinois Chicago; 2University of Illinios and 3University of Illinois at Chicago Background: Candida growth in organ preservation fluid (OPF) is uncommon, with reported incidence ranging up to 4% of OPF. Its clini- cal significance is unclear, as many recipients remain asymptomatic, while on rare occasions, transmission can lead to severe donor-derived infections, most notably mycotic aneurysms, graft loss, and fatal hem- orrhage. The current American Society of Transplantation (AST) guid- ance recommends prompt antifungal therapy when Candida is identified; however, real-world practice patterns and outcomes are not well described. Methods: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of adult solid organ transplant recipients at a tertiary academic center from January 2020 through October 2025. Patients with Candida-positive OPF cultures were identified through the medical rec- ord. We collected recipients' and donors' demographics, microbiological profiles, antifungal management, and clinical outcomes. Invasive can- didiasis was defined as Candida isolated from blood or deep tissue/fluid within 90 days of transplant. Results: We identified 55 solid organ transplant recipients with Candida-positive OPF cultures (34 Kidney, 9 Liver, 12 Kidney-Pancreas). The most common isolates (37 patients) were C. albicans and C. glabrata. Treatment patterns and outcomes var- ied by organ type. Among Kidney recipients, 20.5% (7/34) received no antifungal therapy; notably, none of these untreated patients developed invasive candidiasis, graft loss, or vascular complications. All Liver recipients (n=9) received antifungal therapy, predominantly for <7 days (n=8). Despite treatment, Liver recipients had high morbidity: 22% (2/ 9) progressed to invasive candidiasis (peritonitis and vascular arteritis), and 67% (6/9) demonstrated vascular Doppler abnormalities. Median length of hospital stay was similar across treatment durations (p < 0.05) and similarly no increased readmission rate among all transplant groups. Conclusion: Our findings suggest that the risk of Candida-pos- itive OPF is not uniform across organ types, indicating that current uni- versal treatment recommendations may lead to over-treatment in some populations. Kidney recipients demonstrated favorable outcomes even without antifungal therapy. In contrast, liver recipients remained at risk for significant vascular morbidity and invasive infection regardless of treatment. Shifting to an organ-specific, risk-stratified management strategy can improve antifungal stewardship while ensuring safety for higher-risk recipients. analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to evaluate the progress and effectiveness of an infection prevention and control (IPC) project in healthcare facilities (HCFs) to improve IPC practices and reduce healthcare-associated infections (HAIs).
analysis.study_design_and_population: A comparative cross-sectional design was utilized to collect data through focus group discussions (FGDs), key informant interviews (KIIs), and quantitative knowledge assessments and practice observations. Ten HCFs were selected purposively to have variation on location, IPC performance, and level of convenience sampling was used to select staff.
analysis.methods: Quantitative data were analyzed using STATA 14 software and thematic analysis was conducted for qualitative data. A comparison of SBMR results at baseline (September 2021) and endline (October 2023) was completed to assess effectiveness of the project.
analysis.main_results: The SBMR baseline to endline comparison showed IPC performance increased for 95% of HCFs, from 49.9% to 70.7%, on average. During knowledge assessments participants verbally described accurate knowledge of IPC practices 28.0% of the time, with a higher proportion of participants from rural districts (40.8%) and medical doctors (55.6%) describing practices accurately.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that although the comparison of baseline and endline SBMR results shows progress, IPC knowledge and adherence to evidence-based practices remain low three years into the IPC project, further hindered by insufficient infrastructure and resources.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform the development of targeted IPC interventions, particularly in resource-limited settings, to improve adherence to evidence-based practices and address infrastructure gaps.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on self-reported data and the lack of a follow-up audit at one hospital. The evidence is moderate as it is based on a cross-sectional design and observational data.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the progress and effectiveness of an infection prevention and control (IPC) project across ten healthcare facilities (HCFs) in improving IPC practices. Using a comparative cross-sectional design, data were collected through focus group discussions, key informant interviews, and knowledge assessments. The SBMR results showed an increase in IPC performance from 49.9% to 70.7% on average, with higher accuracy in knowledge among participants from rural districts and medical doctors. However, the authors noted that IPC knowledge and adherence to evidence-based practices remain low, hindered by insufficient infrastructure and resources. The study's findings suggest the need for targeted interventions and improved resource allocation to sustain IPC progress. The evidence is moderate due to the observational nature of the study and the lack of follow-up data at one facility.

full_text: Background: Environmental hygiene (EH) plays a critical role in reducing healthcare-associated infection (HAI) risk, yet significant variability persists in hospital patient room cleaning and disinfection. While discharge cleaning compliance is frequently studied, real-world practices during daily occupied patient room cleaning remain poorly characterized. Furthermore, the time to complete Environmental Services (EVS) tasks is rarely reported in published literature, despite being linked to budget, facility throughput, and patient and employee satisfaction. Researchers conducted a multi-hospital, observational study about environmental cleaning processes. Methods: Across 3 large (<500 beds) teaching hospitals in 3 distinct US regions, researchers shadowed EVS technicians during daily and discharge patient room cleaning across diverse ward types. Direct practice observations documented total turnover time, time to complete tasks such as cleaning the patient and bathroom room surfaces, floor mopping and non-disinfection tasks using a standardized data collection tool (Figure 1). Cleaning compliance was also measured via visual assessment, defined as wiping a surface with a disinfectant wipe or cloth. Results: A total of 638 daily and 91 discharge cleans were evaluated. The average occupied daily room turnover time was 9 minutes. However, square footage, isolation needs, in-room equipment and EVS expectations varied across unit types and individual facilities. For daily occupied room cleaning, on average, more time was spent on non-disinfection tasks like removing waste, refilling consumables and patient engagement (see Table 1). High-touch surface (HTS) cleaning compliance during daily cleans was low (38–48%), whereas floor mopping occurred in <90% of rooms. Site Z spent approximately twice the average time performing a daily room clean compared to Sites X and Y, however, did not achieve greater than 50% HTS cleaning compliance. Discharge cleaning demonstrated markedly higher HTS compliance (87–92%) and longer average duration (Table 2). Conclusion: To date, EH research has been focused on cleaning compliance measured by fluorescent marking, ATP swabbing and/or environmental culturing. Less research, however, is available regarding daily occupied patient room cleaning and the time and resources needed to do it successfully. Our research revealed that EVS technicians across 3 large hospitals spent an average of 9 minutes on daily room cleaning and only a third of that time spent using a disinfectant. Many healthcare disinfectants used by EVS have a contact time of 5 minutes or more. Healthcare leadership should have realistic expectations of what can be accomplished in budgeted cleaning time and the impact of time on disinfectant efficacy, regulatory compliance and infection prevention.A form for observing and recording room cleaning activities in a healthcare setting. analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to develop a measles flagging system within the electronic health record to improve measles surveillance and management. It conducted an observational investigation across three US teaching hospitals, shadowing Environmental Services (EVS) technicians during daily and discharge patient room cleaning. The researchers documented total turnover time and specific tasks, finding that the average daily room cleaning took 9 minutes, with only a third of that time spent on disinfectant use. The findings suggest that current EH research has focused on compliance metrics but lacks attention to the practical challenges of daily cleaning. The evidence is moderate in strength due to the observational design and potential variability in technician performance.

Follow-up studies should employ longer wastewater sampling windows and further refine methods to account for community-associated SARS- CoV-2 contributions to hospital wastewater, an area of active investigation by our group. S1):s186–s187 doi:10.1017/ash.2026.10730 Presentation Type: Poster Presentation Subject Category: Surveillance Abstract ID: 247 Getting Ready for the Storm: A Taskforce Approach to Measles Readiness Sonia Srikanth1, Patrick Ching2, Barry Rittmann2, Yvette Major3, Connie Atkinson4, Jenna Price5, Alexandra Bryson, Christopher Doern, Kaila Cooper6 and Michelle Doll2 1VCU School of Medicine; 2Virginia Commonwealth University; 3VCUHS; 4Children's Hospital of Richmond at VCU Health; 5VCU Health Healthcare Infection Prevention Program and 6Nursing VCU Health Background: Identified risk factors for Candida auris infection are gener- ally markers of disease severity and/or medical vulnerability. A regional C. auris outbreak in 2022 led to extensive admission and point-prevalence testing in tertiary care hospital. We retrospectively reviewed charts to iden- tify novel risk factors for progression from colonization to infection in a universally medically complex population. Methods: A case-control study was performed to compare patients developing invasive infection (cases) from those remaining colonization. Inclusion criteria were patients newly identified to be colonized with C. auris during a hospital admission from 1/ 2023 through 5/2025. Patients diagnosed with clinical infection as their first evidence of colonization were excluded. Risk factor variables included ICU status, other drug resistant organisms (MDROs), length of stay (LOS), time to colonization (days from admission to identification of C. auris), antimicrobial coverage with broadly acting agents, operative and other procedures, type/number of devices. Factors were compared between cases and controls using Fisher’s Exact Tests for categorical variables and Mann- Whitney U Tests for continuous variables using SAS 9.4. Results: During the study, 74 patients became colonized and 17 went on to develop invasive infection. The following were associated with infection: colonization with other MDROs, tracheostomy, liver failure, dialysis (though not renal fail- ure), transplant w/in last year (driven by liver, N=7), number of drains at colonization (table 1). Several factors associated with severity of illness (ICU status, antibiotic pressure) were not associated with progression to infection in this cohort. Discussion: In a medically complex population, several risk factors associated with illness severity were not associated with progression from C. auris colonization to infection, whereas liver disease and transplantation, along with other MDROs, tracheostomy, and number of drains were. Targeted interventions attempting to decolonize trache- ostomy or drain sites, and/or liver disease patients in general may help pri- oritize infection prevention where it is most needed. analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to identify risk factors for progression from Candida auris colonization to infection in a medically complex population, addressing a gap in understanding how to prioritize infection prevention strategies.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A case-control study was conducted comparing patients who developed invasive infection with those who remained colonized, focusing on patients newly identified with C. auris colonization during hospital admissions from January 2023 through May 2025.
analysis.methods: The study retrospectively reviewed medical charts to identify risk factors, using Fisher’s Exact Tests for categorical variables and Mann-Whitney U Tests for continuous variables, with statistical analysis performed using SAS 9.4.
analysis.main_results: During the study, 74 patients became colonized with C. auris, and 17 developed invasive infection. Factors associated with infection included colonization with other MDROs, tracheostomy, liver failure, dialysis, transplant within the last year (especially liver transplants), and the number of drains at colonization.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: In a medically complex population, several risk factors associated with illness severity were not linked to progression from C. auris colonization to infection, whereas liver disease, transplantation, tracheostomy, and the number of drains were significantly associated.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings may inform targeted infection prevention strategies, particularly for patients with tracheostomy, drains, liver disease, or recent transplants, where intervention could be most effective.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study was limited by small HAI sample sizes and a short wastewater sampling period, which may affect the generalizability of the findings. However, the evidence is considered moderate due to the retrospective design and statistical analysis.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to identify risk factors for progression from Candida auris colonization to infection in a medically complex population. A case-control study was conducted on 74 colonized patients and 17 who developed invasive infection, comparing factors such as ICU status, presence of other drug-resistant organisms, tracheostomy, liver failure, dialysis, and number of drains. The results showed that colonization with other MDROs, tracheostomy, liver failure, dialysis, transplant within the last year (especially liver transplants), and the number of drains were associated with infection. The authors interpreted that while factors like ICU status and antibiotic pressure were not linked to infection progression, liver disease, transplantation, and other MDROs were significant. These findings may guide targeted infection prevention strategies in high-risk groups. However, the study's small sample size and short sampling period limit the confidence in the results, leading to a moderate evidence assessment.

full_text: AbstractBackground: With increasing utilization of oral antibiotics in serious infections, complex outpatient antimicrobial therapy (COpAT) programs are vital for improving patient safety and outcomes. We discuss the Michigan Medicine (MM) COpAT program, including processes, interventions, and evaluate its impact. Methods: Adult patients discharged from MM hospital between Jan-Oct 2025 were eligible for COpAT program enrollment if prescribed antibiotics for ≥14 days, including oral antibiotics requiring lab monitoring, long-acting lipoglycopeptides, or intravenous (IV) antibiotics administered at a hemodialysis center, subacute nursing facility, or home. Eligible diagnoses include osteomyelitis, prosthetic joint infection, septic joint, spinal hardware infection and infectious tenosynovitis. Established in October 2024, the COpAT program consists of an infectious diseases (ID) pharmacist with ID physician oversight. The pharmacist conducts a telephone-encounter within 2 business days of discharge to review antibiotic plan, lab monitoring, appropriate antibiotic administration, duration and adherence, and assess for adverse effects. The outpatient ID physician is notified of treatment concerns and lab monitoring results. Another telephone-encounter occurs 2 weeks post-discharge to re-evaluate antibiotic therapy. COpAT patient outcomes and process measures were compared to a historical cohort of patients discharged from MM on oral or IV antibiotics for an osteoarticular infection from May – August 2023. Chi-squared tests were used for categorical variables; the Mann-Whitney U test was used to compare median length of stay (LOS). Results: From January-October 2025, 163 patients with osteoarticular infections were enrolled in COpAT post-discharge. There were 124 patients in the historical cohort. Among COpAT patients, 79.8% (130/163) were discharged on oral antibiotics compared to 33.9% (42/124) in the historical cohort (p<0.0001, Figure 1). COpAT patients had a shorter median LOS of 6.1 days [IQR 4.2-8.7] versus 8.2 days [IQR 5.3-12.1, p<0.0001], and numerical reduction of 30-day readmission rate of 12% (19/158) versus 16.9% (22/132) in the historical cohort (p=0.258). In a subset of 85 patients enrolled from 1/1– 5/31/25, 96.5% had a COpAT telephone-encounter within 2 business days and 638 pharmacist interventions occurred with an average 7.4 interventions/patient (Figure 2). Conclusion: COpAT patients had significantly increased oral antibiotic utilization and shorter LOS, and numerically fewer readmissions compared to a historic cohort. The increase in oral and long-acting antibiotics, rapid post-discharge follow-up and multiple COpAT pharmacist interventions likely contributed to improved outcomes and safer transitions of care. COpAT programs should be instituted to improve patient outcomes and ensure safe use of oral and IV antibiotics in serious infections.A bar graph comparing oral and long-acting antibiotics versus intravenous antibiotics for osteoarticular infections. A bar graph showing pharmacist interventions over five months.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addresses the need for safe transitions of care for patients requiring prolonged outpatient antibiotic therapy, highlighting gaps in monitoring and follow-up after hospital discharge for serious infections.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A retrospective cohort study compared outcomes of patients enrolled in the Michigan Medicine Complex Outpatient Antimicrobial Therapy (COpAT) program from January to October 2025 with a historical cohort discharged on antibiotics for osteoarticular infections between May and August 2023.
analysis.methods: Eligible patients were adults discharged on antibiotics for ≥14 days, including oral antibiotics requiring monitoring, long-acting lipoglycopeptides, or IV antibiotics administered at specific settings. An infectious diseases pharmacist conducted telephone encounters within 2 business days and 2 weeks post-discharge to review therapy, monitoring, adherence, and adverse effects, with physician oversight.
analysis.main_results: Among 163 COpAT patients, 79.8% (130/163) were discharged on oral antibiotics versus 33.9% (42/124) in the historical cohort (p<0.0001). COpAT patients had a shorter median length of stay (6.1 days [IQR 4.2–8.7] vs 8.2 days [IQR 5.3–12.1], p<0.0001) and a numerically lower 30-day readmission rate (12% vs 16.9%, p=0.258).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors attribute improved outcomes to increased oral antibiotic use, rapid post-discharge follow-up, and frequent pharmacist interventions, suggesting COpAT programs enhance patient safety and care transitions for serious infections.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings support implementing COpAT programs to improve patient safety and optimize antibiotic use in serious infections, particularly for osteoarticular infections requiring prolonged therapy.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study’s retrospective design, reliance on historical controls, and lack of randomization limit causal inference; generalizability may be constrained by single-center data and specific infection types, warranting moderate confidence.

analysis.summary_en: This retrospective cohort study evaluated the impact of the Michigan Medicine Complex Outpatient Antimicrobial Therapy (COpAT) program on patients discharged with prolonged antibiotic therapy for osteoarticular infections. Compared to a historical cohort, COpAT patients had significantly higher oral antibiotic utilization (79.8% vs 33.9%, p<0.0001) and shorter median hospital stays (6.1 vs 8.2 days, p<0.0001), with a numerically lower 30-day readmission rate (12% vs 16.9%, p=0.258). The program involved structured pharmacist-led telephone follow-up within 2 business days and 2 weeks post-discharge, alongside infectious diseases physician oversight. The authors interpret these findings as evidence that COpAT programs improve patient safety and care transitions by enabling safer use of oral and IV antibiotics. While the results suggest benefits, the study’s retrospective design, single-center setting, and lack of randomization limit causal conclusions, warranting moderate confidence in the evidence.

title: Timeliness of measles vaccination in selected districts of Oromia Region, Ethiopia – 2021
abstract: Background Delays in vaccination with the first/s dose of measles-containing vaccine (MCV1, MCV2) increases risk of measles transmission. MCV2 was added to Ethiopia's routine immunization schedule in 2019, administered at age 15 months. We describe age at measles vaccination and characteristics associated with timely vaccination following MCV2 introduction. Methods A secondary analysis from a 2021 cross-sectional household survey of children aged 12–35 months in Oromia, Ethiopia was conducted. MCV vaccination status and age at vaccination were determined from the child's vaccination card. The cumulative card-confirmed vaccination coverage of MCV1 and MCV2 (among children 24–35 months) by age at vaccination was estimated. Among children who received MCV, vaccination timing was classified as early (MCV1: <9 months; MCV2: <15 months), timely (MCV1: 9 to <10 months; MCV2: 15 to <16 months), or delayed (MCV1: ≥10 months; MCV2: ≥16 months). Characteristics associated with timely MCV1 vaccination were analyzed using multivariate logistic regression, with urban/rural stratification. Results Overall, 651 children aged 12–35 months (MCV1) and a subset of 270 children aged 24–35 months (MCV2) were analyzed. Cumulative MCV1 coverage was 59.9% by age 9 months and 76.3% by age 12 months, and MCV2 was 33.0% by age 15 months and 44.8% by age 24 months. MCV coverage was generally higher in urban compared to rural areas. Among vaccinated children, the proportion receiving early, timely, and delayed doses was 30.1%, 44.5%, and 25.3% for MCV1, and 28.6%, 41.2%, and 30.3% for MCV2, respectively. Characteristics associated with timely MCV1 vaccination differed in urban and rural areas, but common themes included increased caregiver immunization awareness and service delivery aspects. Conclusions Although most children who received MCV1 were vaccinated by 12 months, many received delayed doses. MCV2 coverage was low, irrespective of vaccination timing. Findings highlight the importance of routine catch-up vaccination policies and guidance, and the need for tailored strategies in urban and rural settings to improve MCV coverage and timely vaccination.

elements_zh.methods: MCV 疫苗接种 状态和 疫苗接种 年龄是根据孩子的 疫苗接种 卡确定的。使用多元逻辑回归和城市/农村分层分析与及时 MCV1 疫苗接种 相关的特征。
elements_zh.main_results: 9 个月时的累积 MCV1 覆盖率为 59.9%,12 个月时为 76.3%,15 个月时的 MCV2 累积覆盖率为 33.0%,24 个月时为 44.8%。与农村地区相比,城市地区的 MCV 覆盖率普遍较高。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 与及时 MCV1 疫苗接种 相关的特征在城市和农村地区有所不同,但共同主题包括护理人员免疫意识和服务提供方面的提高。

full_text: The World Health Organization estimates that in 2026 nearly 11 million people will contract the virus that causes measles. Most of these cases will occur in Africa and Asia, but many countries in the Americas and Europe are reporting outbreaks affecting hundreds or thousands of people. There is no treatment for measles, but vaccines have been proven to be safe and effective at preventing the disease. Unvaccinated people who get sick with measles are at risk of serious complications that can lead to deafness, blindness and death. The risk of a bad outcome is higher for people who are undernourished and unable to access supportive medical care. As an infectious disease epidemiologist, I study the reasons for changes in population health risks around the world. The specific factors leading to measles epidemics vary by country, but the underlying cause everywhere is decreased vaccination rates. Zero-dose children in low-income countries The vast majority of parents around the world want to protect their children from preventable infectious diseases through vaccination. In many lower-income countries, the supply of vaccines remains insufficient to meet the demand for them. Because measles is highly contagious, the vaccination rate needs to be above 95% to protect a community from outbreaks, creating what is known as “herd immunity.” One dose of measles vaccine protects most people from the disease, but two doses are recommended to improve effectiveness. Most high-income countries have measles vaccine rates near the 95% target. In Europe, the average one-dose vaccination rate is about 94%, and the two-dose rate is about 88%. In the U.S., more than 90% of 2-year-olds have received at least one dose of measles vaccine and more than 92% of kindergartners have received two doses. The vaccine coverage rate is above 95% in many communities, though it is much lower in some school districts. In contrast, only about 80% of young children in low- and middle-income countries have received at least one dose of measles vaccine, and only about 70% have received two doses. Almost every country had reduced access to vaccines during the early months of the COVID-19 pandemic, when supply chains and clinic access were severely disrupted. Most young children in high-income countries were able to catch up on missed doses before they reached school age. But in lower-income countries, millions of kids who missed routine vaccinations during the pandemic are still classified as “zero-dose children” who have not received any of the vaccines their countries recommend. Only a tiny fraction of the cases of measles diagnosed in lower-income countries are confirmed with laboratory tests and reported to public health authorities, so it’s impossible to get an exact case count. But healthcare workers have reported observing higher than typical numbers of cases in many countries during the past year. In 2026, measles epidemics have been reported in countries experiencing armed conflict or housing refugees displaced by war, such as Burundi, Democratic Republic of Congo, Somalia, Sudan and Yemen. Outbreaks have also been reported in peaceful countries, including Maldives and Zambia, and cases are surging in India. Dozens of other countries are also experiencing epidemics. All of these situations are linked to undervaccination. Vaccine shortages in Bangladesh Bangladesh has reported more measles cases this year than any other country, and more than 900 people have died from the infection. While Bangladesh faces many of the same challenges as other low- and middle-income countries, the past few years have presented some unique difficulties. In 2024, the country’s longtime government collapsed and an interim government was installed. During this time of political instability the government ordered too few vaccine doses. In 2025 vaccine shortages worsened when the interim government decided to stop procuring its vaccines through UNICEF and instead tried to purchase them through a competitive bidding process before new supply chains had been established. Bangladesh has now resumed working with UNICEF to acquire vaccines. Unfortunately, it has returned to UNICEF at a time when its partner organization Gavi, the Vaccine Alliance, is facing funding cuts. Under Gavi’s cofinancing model, low- and middle-income countries’ initial vaccine purchases are subsidized by contributions from high-income countries and other investors. Over time, countries pay an increasing portion of their own vaccine costs. Because Gavi pools orders from all over the world, it is able to shape markets and negotiate with vaccine manufacturers for lower costs per dose. The major limitation of this system is that reduced funding for global health shrinks the budget for subsidizing vaccine purchases. But since 2025, France, Germany, the U.K., the U.S. and several other high-income countries have significantly reduced their budgets for development assistance, leaving Gavi with a substantial budget shortfall. As Bangladesh has grown its economy, it is paying a greater share of the costs of the vaccines it purchases through Gavi. However, it does not yet have the means to fully self-finance its vaccine program. For now, if Gavi’s budget is not fully replenished, countries like Bangladesh will not have enough money to buy all of the vaccines they need. Even though a mass vaccination campaign in early 2026 saw more than 1 million Bangladeshi children vaccinated against measles, the percentage of children who have been vaccinated remains far below the 95% threshold required to prevent widespread epidemics. Vaccine hesitancy in faith communities in the Americas Two years ago the entire region of the Americas – North, Central, and South America and the Caribbean – was classified as a measles-free zone. Canada officially lost its measles elimination status in November 2025 after more than a year of sustained transmission. Mexico and the U.S. have met the criteria to lose their measles-free status when the Pan American Health Organization’s measles elimination committee meets again in November 2026. The country reporting the largest number of measles cases in the Americas in 2026 is Guatemala, which has already logged more than 30,000 confirmed cases. The Guatemalan epidemic has been traced back to a gathering in Santiago Atitlán in December 2025 that was organized by a Christian megachurch whose leaders have been vocal about their anti-vaccine views. Measles began circulating in late 2024 and early 2025 in Canada, Mexico and the U.S. among rural, conservative Mennonite communities where leaving children unvaccinated has become the cultural norm. In South Carolina and Utah, recent outbreaks have been linked to low vaccination rates among conservative religious groups that are not connected with Mennonite churches. More cases of measles have already been diagnosed in the U.S. in 2026 than in any year since 1991. The measles virus has moved from religious communities into other undervaccinated population groups. The epidemic that started in Mennonite villages in Mexico spread into neighboring Indigenous communities. An outbreak that started among German-speaking Mennonites in Bolivia crossed the border into Peru and was then amplified by visitors to large cultural festivals who brought the virus home with them. Stopping the spread The total number of measles cases per year decreased from an estimated 38 million in 2000 to about 10 million in 2019. That trend has reversed since the COVID-19 pandemic. The number of measles cases and the number of countries experiencing measles epidemics has gone up as the vaccination rate in some populations has gone down. Getting back on track toward eliminating measles as a global public health problem will look different depending on the circumstances in each country. For low- and middle-income countries, ending measles epidemics will require increasing funding for Gavi and other international partnerships so that the vaccine supply can grow to meet the demand. The need is different in countries where vaccination rates are falling even though measles vaccines are readily available. Stopping the spread of measles in undervaccinated communities will depend on the challenging task of building vaccine confidence among parents of young children.

title_original: Why millions of people around the world will contract measles in 2026

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addresses the global public health concern of rising measles cases in 2026, highlighting the need to understand the factors contributing to this increase and the associated risks.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study is a global epidemiological analysis conducted in 2026, examining measles cases across various regions, including Africa, Asia, the Americas, and Europe, with a focus on countries experiencing outbreaks and disparities in vaccination rates.
analysis.methods: The study uses global health data, including vaccination coverage rates, outbreak reports, and public health observations, to identify trends and factors influencing measles transmission and incidence.
analysis.main_results: The study found that measles epidemics in 2026 are linked to decreased vaccination rates, with specific cases reported in countries affected by conflict and in peaceful countries like the Maldives and Zambia. In Bangladesh, vaccine shortages and funding issues have contributed to a significant rise in measles cases and deaths.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret that the underlying cause of measles epidemics globally is the decline in vaccination rates, and they note that the situation varies by country due to differing circumstances and challenges.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform the importance of maintaining high vaccination rates to prevent outbreaks and highlight the need for targeted interventions in low-income countries and regions with political instability.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is limited by the lack of exact case counts in many lower-income countries, as only a small fraction of measles cases are confirmed through laboratory tests. analysis.summary_en: This study highlights the global resurgence of measles in 2026, driven by decreased vaccination rates in various regions. source_body_en: As an infectious disease epidemiologist, I study the reasons for changes in population health risks around the world. The World Health Organization estimates that in 2026 nearly 11 million people will contract the virus that causes measles. Most of these cases will occur in Africa and Asia, but many countries in the Americas and Europe are reporting outbreaks affecting hundreds or thousands of people. There is no treatment for measles, but vaccines have been proven to be safe and effective at preventing the disease. Unvaccinated people who get sick with measles are at risk of serious complications that can lead to deafness, blindness and death. The risk of a bad outcome is higher for people who are undernourished and unable to access supportive medical care. The specific factors leading to measles epidemics vary by country, but the underlying cause everywhere is decreased vaccination rates. Zero-dose children in low-income countries The vast majority of parents around the world want to protect their children from preventable infectious diseases through vaccination. In many lower-income countries, the supply of vaccines remains insufficient to meet the demand for them. Because measles is highly contagious, the vaccination rate needs to be above 95% to protect a community from outbreaks, creating what is known as “herd immunity.” One dose of measles vaccine protects most people from the disease, but two doses are recommended to improve effectiveness. Most high-income countries have measles vaccine rates near the 95% target. In Europe, the average one-dose vaccination rate is about 94%, and the two-dose rate is about 88%. In the U.S., more than 90% of 2-year-olds have received at least one dose of measles vaccine and more than 92% of kindergartners have received two doses.

media_mentions.content: U.S. News World News Korea Regional Review Latin America Region Odd News Entertainment Movies Music TV Sports NFL MLB NBA Soccer Voices Photos News US News World News Entertainment Sports Archive Almanac Voices Aug. 21, 2026 / 11:17 AM Why millions of people around the world will contract measles in 2026 By Kathryn H. Jacobsen, University of Richmond The World Health Organization estimates that in 2026 nearly 11 million people will contract the virus that causes measles. File Photo by Annie Rice/EPA-EFE The World Health Organization estimates that in 2026 nearly 11 million people will contract the virus that causes measles. Most of these cases will occur in Africa and Asia, but many countries in the Americas and Europe are reporting outbreaks affecting hundreds or thousands of people. There is no treatment for measles, but vaccines have been proven to be safe and effective at preventing the disease. Unvaccinated people who get sick with measles are at risk of serious complications that can lead to deafness, blindness and death. The risk of a bad outcome is higher for people who are undernourished and unable to access supportive medical care. As an infectious disease epidemiologist, I study the reasons for changes in population health risks around the world. The specific factors leading to measles epidemics vary by country, but the underlying cause everywhere is decreased vaccination rates. Zero-dose children in low-income countries The vast majority of parents around the world want to protect their children from preventable infectious diseases through vaccination. In many lower-income countries, the supply of vaccines remains insufficient to meet the demand for them. Because measles is highly contagious, the vaccination rate needs to be above 95% to protect a community from outbreaks, creating what is known as "herd immunity." One dose of measles vaccine protects most people from the disease, but two doses are recommended to improve effectiveness. Most high-income countries have measles vaccine rates near the 95% target. In Europe, the average one-dose vaccination rate is about 94%, and the two-dose rate is about 88%. In the U.S., more than 90% of 2-year-olds have received at least one dose of measles vaccine and more than 92% of kindergartners have received two doses. The vaccine coverage rate is above 95% in many communities, though it is much lower in some school districts. In contrast, only about 80% of young children in low- and middle-income countries have received at least one dose of measles vaccine, and only about 70% have received two doses. Almost every country had reduced access to vaccines during the early months of the COVID-19 pandemic, when supply chains and clinic access were severely disrupted. Most young children in high-income countries were able to catch up on missed doses before they reached school age. But in lower-income countries, millions of kids who missed routine vaccinations during the pandemic are still classified as "zero-dose children" who have not received any of the vaccines their countries recommend. Only a tiny fraction of the cases of measles diagnosed in lower-income countries are confirmed with laboratory tests and reported to public health authorities, so it's impossible to get an exact case count. But healthcare workers have reported observing higher than typical numbers of cases in many countries during the past year. In 2026, measles epidemics have been reported in countries experiencing armed conflict or housing refugees displaced by war, such as Burundi, Democratic Republic of Congo, Somalia, Sudan and Yemen. Outbreaks have also been reported in peaceful countries, including Maldives and Zambia, and cases are surging in India. Dozens of other countries are also experiencing epidemics. All of these situations are linked to undervaccination. Vaccine shortages in Bangladesh Bangladesh has reported more measles cases this year than any other country, and more than 900 people have died from the infection. While Bangladesh faces many of the same challenges as other low- and middle-income countries, the past few years have presented some unique difficulties. In 2024, the country's longtime government collapsed and an interim government was installed. During this time of political instability the government ordered too few vaccine doses. In 2025 vaccine shortages worsened when the interim government decided to stop procuring its vaccines through UNICEF and instead tried to purchase them through a competitive bidding process before new supply chains had been established. Bangladesh has now resumed working with UNICEF to acquire vaccines. Unfortunately, it has returned to UNICEF at a time when its partner organization Gavi, the Vaccine Alliance, is facing funding cuts. Under Gavi's cofinancing model, low- and middle-income countries' initial vaccine purchases are subsidized by contributions from high-income countries and other investors. Over time, countries pay an increasing portion of their own vaccine costs. Because Gavi pools orders from all over the world, it is able to shape markets and negotiate with vaccine manufacturers for lower costs per dose. The major limitation of this system is that reduced funding for global health shrinks the budget for subsidizing vaccine purchases. The ongoing measles outbreak in Bangladesh is the result of a unique combination of political upheaval and a shortage of vaccines. But since 2025, France, Germany, the U.K., the U.S. and several other high-income countries have significantly reduced their budgets for development assistance, leaving Gavi with a substantial budget shortfall. As Bangladesh has grown its economy, it is paying a greater share of the costs of the vaccines it purchases through Gavi. However, it does not yet have the means to fully self-finance its vaccine program. For now, if Gavi's budget is not fully replenished, countries like Bangladesh will not have enough money to buy all of the vaccines they need. Even though a mass vaccination campaign in early 2026 saw more than 1 million Bangladeshi children vaccinated against measles, the percentage of children who have been vaccinated remains far below the 95% threshold required to prevent widespread epidemics. Vaccine hesitancy in faith communities in the Americas Two years ago the entire region of the Americas -- North, Central, and South America and the Caribbean -- was classified as a measles-free zone. Canada officially lost its measles elimination status in November 2025 after more than a year of sustained transmission. Mexico and the U.S. have met the criteria to lose their measles-free status when the Pan American Health Organization's measles elimination committee meets again in November 2026. The country reporting the largest number of measles cases in the Americas in 2026 is Guatemala, which has already logged more than 30,000 confirmed cases. The Guatemalan epidemic has been traced back to a gathering in Santiago Atitlán in December 2025 that was organized by a Christian megachurch whose leaders have been vocal about their anti-vaccine views. Measles began circulating in late 2024 and early 2025 in Canada, Mexico and the U.S. among rural, conservative Mennonite communities where leaving children unvaccinated has become the cultural norm. In South Carolina and Utah, recent outbreaks have been linked to low vaccination rates among conservative religious groups that are not connected with Mennonite churches. More cases of measles have already been diagnosed in the U.S. in 2026 than in any year since 1991. The measles virus has moved from religious communities into other undervaccinated population groups. The epidemic that started in Mennonite villages in Mexico spread into neighboring Indigenous communities. An outbreak that started among German-speaking Mennonites in Bolivia crossed the border into Peru and was then amplified by visitors to large cultural festivals who brought the virus home with them. Stopping the spread The total number of measles cases per year decreased from an estimated 38 million in 2000 to about 10 million in 2019. That trend has reversed since the COVID-19 pandemic. The number of measles cases and the number of countries experiencing measles epidemics has gone up as the vaccination rate in some populations has gone down. Getting back on track toward eliminating measles as a global public health problem will look different depending on the circumstances in each country. For low- and middle-income countries, ending measles epidemics will require increasing funding for Gavi and other international partnerships so that the vaccine supply can grow to meet the demand. The need is different in countries where vaccination rates are falling even though measles vaccines are readily available. Stopping the spread of measles in undervaccinated communities will depend on the challenging task of building vaccine confidence among parents of young children. Kathryn H. full_text: Serum Institute of India MMR, a lower-cost vaccine, was low and consis- tent with other reports. No cases of aseptic meningitis were reported. With the rising number of measles cases worldwide and the need to increase vac- cination coverage against measles in under-vaccinated populations, reinforcing the similar efficacy and safety of different vaccines is crucial. All HCWs must be protected. Antimicrobial Stewardship & Healthcare Epidemiology 2026;6(Suppl. S1):s191–s192 doi:10.1017/ash.2026.10739 Presentation Type: Poster Presentation Subject Category: VAE Abstract ID: 360 Antimicrobial Resistance Surveillance in the Cuautla River, Mexico Nicole Jackson1 MSOL, CIC, Atrium Health Navicent Background: Ventilator-associated events (VAEs) are episodes of respira- tory deterioration after stability during mechanical ventilation, posing sig- nificant risks for morbidity and mortality. Extremely low birth weight neonates (<750 g), particularly those born at 22–24 weeks gestation, are highly vulnerable. In our Neonatal Intensive Care Unit (NICU), eight VAEs occurred in the previous year, leading to prolonged ventilation, increased infection risk, and higher mortality. Reducing VAEs is essential for improving patient safety, health equity, and family experience while meeting NHSN benchmarks and regulatory goals. Methods: A structured, evidence-based approach was implemented using failure mode effects analysis (FMEA) to identify risk factors and guide interventions. A multi- disciplinary team developed a formalized VAE prevention bundle, which included: - Formation of a multidisciplinary task force - Process measures tied to critical clinical tasks - Creation of an EHR tool for real-time com- pliance monitoring - Staff education and workflow alignment - Cultural engagement initiatives to reinforce best practices Pre- and post-interven- tion data were collected and analyzed for neonates <750 g per NHSN guidelines. Result: Post-implementation, VAE rates decreased from 9.8 to zero per 1,000 ventilator days, achieving an SIR ?1.0 and meeting national benchmarks. Mortality among extremely low birth weight neo- nates declined by 60%. Integration of EHR visualization and Power BI dashboards enabled real-time monitoring and sustained compliance. The initiative generated an estimated annual cost savings of $2.1 million through reduced length of stay and infection-related expenses. Conclusion: Structured care bundles, integrated data tools, and multidis- ciplinary engagement can eliminate VAEs in high-risk neonates. Broader adoption across NICUs could enhance patient safety, reduce healthcare costs, and improve outcomes systemwide. Innovative clinical practice plays a pivotal role in sustaining these improvements through adherence to pre- vention bundles, leveraging technology for real-time compliance, and fos- tering a culture of accountability. Standardized frameworks and education strategies can be scaled across institutions for continuous improvement. References Bondarev DJ, Ryan RM, Mukherjee D. (2024). The spectrum of pneumonia among intubated neonates in the neonatal intensive care unit. analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address the rising global measles cases and the need to increase vaccination coverage in under-vaccinated populations by reinforcing the similar efficacy and safety of different measles vaccines.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to address the rising global measles cases and the need to increase vaccination coverage in under-vaccinated populations by reinforcing the similar efficacy and safety of different measles vaccines. A multi-disciplinary team implemented a structured, evidence-based approach using failure mode effects analysis (FMEA) to identify risk factors and guide interventions in a Neonatal Intensive Care Unit (NICU) focusing on extremely low birth weight neonates (<750 g). The methods included the formation of a multidisciplinary task force, process measures tied to critical clinical tasks, creation of an EHR tool for real-time compliance monitoring, staff education and workflow alignment, and cultural engagement initiatives. Pre- and post-intervention data were collected and analyzed for neonates <750 g per NHSN guidelines. The main results showed that post-implementation, VAE rates decreased from 9.8 to zero per 1,000 ventilator days, achieving an SIR ?1.0 and meeting national benchmarks. Mortality among extremely low birth weight neonates declined by 60%. The authors interpreted these results as evidence that structured care bundles, integrated data tools, and multidisciplinary engagement can eliminate VAEs in high-risk neonates, which is a novel finding in the context of neonatal care. The findings can inform strategies to improve patient safety, reduce healthcare costs, and enhance outcomes systemwide by implementing standardized frameworks and education strategies across NICUs. The study is limited by its focus on a single NICU, which may affect generalisability, but the evidence is strong as it demonstrates a significant reduction in VAE rates and mortality through targeted interventions.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在通过加强不同 麻疹 疫苗 的相似功效和安全性来解决全球 麻疹 病例不断上升的问题,以及提高疫苗接种不足人群中 麻疹 覆盖率的需要。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 多学科团队采用失败模式效应分析 (FMEA) 实施结构化、基于证据的方法,以识别风险因素并指导新生儿重症监护病房 (NICU) 的干预措施,重点关注极低出生体重新生儿 (<750 g)。
elements_zh.methods: 制定了正式的 VAE 预防包,包括组建多学科工作组、与关键临床任务相关的流程措施、创建用于实时合规性监控的 EHR 工具、员工教育和工作流程调整以及文化参与举措。根据 NHSN 指南,收集并分析 <750 g 新生儿的干预前和干预后数据。
elements_zh.main_results: 实施后,VAE 率从每 1,000 个呼吸机日 9.8 降至零,实现 SIR 1.0 并达到国家基准。极低出生体重新生儿的 死亡率 下降了 60%。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将结果解释为结构化护理组合、综合数据工具和多学科参与可以消除高危新生儿 VAE 的证据,这是新生儿护理领域的一个新发现。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果可以为改善患者安全、降低医疗成本以及通过在新生儿重症监护病房实施标准化框架和教育策略来提高全系统结果的策略提供参考。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究因其关注单一新生儿重症监护病房(NICU)而受到限制,这可能会影响普遍性。然而,证据是强有力的,因为它表明通过有针对性的干预措施可以显着降低 VAE 率和 死亡率。

analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 多学科团队采用失败模式效应分析 (FMEA) 实施结构化、基于证据的方法,以识别风险因素并指导新生儿重症监护病房 (NICU) 的干预措施,重点关注极低出生体重新生儿 (<750 g)。
analysis_zh.methods: 制定了正式的 VAE 预防包,包括组建多学科工作组、与关键临床任务相关的流程措施、创建用于实时合规性监控的 EHR 工具、员工教育和工作流程调整以及文化参与举措。根据 NHSN 指南,收集并分析 <750 g 新生儿的干预前和干预后数据。
analysis_zh.main_results: 实施后,VAE 率从每 1,000 个呼吸机日 9.8 降至零,实现 SIR 1.0 并达到国家基准。极低出生体重新生儿的 死亡率 下降了 60%。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将结果解释为结构化护理组合、综合数据工具和多学科参与可以消除高危新生儿 VAE 的证据,这是新生儿护理领域的一个新发现。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果可以为改善患者安全、降低医疗成本以及通过在新生儿重症监护病房实施标准化框架和教育策略来提高全系统结果的策略提供参考。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究因其关注单一新生儿重症监护病房(NICU)而受到限制,这可能会影响普遍性。然而,证据是强有力的,因为它表明通过有针对性的干预措施可以显着降低 VAE 率和 死亡率。

full_text: Presentation Type: Poster Presentation Subject Category: Outbreaks Abstract ID: 333 Institutional and Behavioral Determinants of Sharps Injury Reporting and Protective Equipment Use in Nursing Professionals in Croatia Teppei Shimasaki1 Kyorin University Background: Trypan blue is commonly used during mature cataract sur- gery to improve visualization of the anterior capsule. Although FDA- approved since 2004, it remains unapproved in Japan. Many clinics per- form sterile filtration prior to use; however, no standardized sterilization protocol exists. Methods: This retrospective case series included all patients diagnosed with Sarocladium kiliense endophthalmitis after cata- ract surgery at Kyorin University Hospital between 2015 and 2025. Results: In 2025, six microbiologically confirmed cases of S. kiliense endophthalmitis were identified; none occurred before 2024. One case originated from Clinic A and five from Clinic B. All cataract surgeries used trypan blue, which had been sterile-filtered at each institution. Discussion: Endophthalmitis is a rare postoperative complication of cataract surgery, and S. kiliense is an uncommon pathogen. We were informed that similar cases occurred sporadically in 2025 from a reference laboratory center. One institution confirmed contamination of the trypan blue product (unpub- lished data). The same organism was isolated from dye obtained from Clinic B. All affected clinics used trypan blue from the same manufacturer. Off-label product use may pose significant safety concerns due to limited data. While other off-label dyes (e.g., Lugol’s solution, India ink) are widely used in Japan, they are applied superficially. We hypothesize that contami- nated trypan blue migrated into the vitreous cavity via lens zonules, caus- ing the outbreak. Physicians bear responsibility for off-label use and should employ unapproved products only when benefits clearly outweigh risks. Antimicrobial Stewardship & Healthcare Epidemiology 2026;6(Suppl. As a highly infectious virus with an estimated R ranging from 12-18, we sought rapidly scalable and implementable mea- sles preparedness measures for our facilities. Methods: The electronic health record (EHR) has flags that can be placed on patient records to denote the presence of, or concern for, active, transmissible infections. These flags are highly visible in the EHR and represent a good usability heuristic as front line providers are already trained to look for this infor- mation. Infection Prevention and Control (IPAC) worked with nursing informatics to develop measles-specific flags for suspected, confirmed and exposed patients in the EHR, expanding flagging functionality in preparation for potential measles cases and exposures. The flagging was tied to registry functionality to allow for tracking of exposed and confirmed cases longitudinally for supporting IPAC investigations in addition to clinical operations. Results: Three different flags were developed in the EHR to address measles. Specific criteria were created for each flag, as shown in Table 1. Table 1: Attached as Image Conclusion: As a highly con- tagious virus, measles presents unique challenges to healthcare facilities managing both cases and exposures. Measles flags within the EHR can be leveraged to assist facilities with case tracking, exposure management, and infection prevention and control. analysis.research_question_and_background: In 2025, measles outbreaks drove 87% of confirmed cases in the United States, highlighting the need for rapidly scalable preparedness measures in healthcare facilities.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study was conducted at Mayo Clinic facilities, where Infection Prevention and Control (IPAC) collaborated with nursing informatics to develop measles-specific electronic health record (EHR) flags for suspected, confirmed, and exposed patients.
analysis.methods: The EHR flags were designed to be highly visible and integrated with registry functionality to enable longitudinal tracking of exposed and confirmed cases, supporting infection prevention and control investigations and clinical operations.
analysis.main_results: Three distinct measles-specific flags were developed in the EHR, each with specific criteria for use as outlined in Table 1.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret the EHR flags as a novel and implementable tool to assist facilities in case tracking, exposure management, and infection prevention and control during measles outbreaks.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Measles flags within the EHR can inform infection prevention strategies by improving case tracking, exposure management, and real-time response capabilities in healthcare settings.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The supplied evidence does not report the effectiveness of the EHR flags in reducing measles transmission or improving clinical outcomes, limiting the strength of the evidence to a descriptive implementation study.

analysis.summary_en: This study describes the development and implementation of measles-specific electronic health record (EHR) flags at Mayo Clinic to support infection prevention and control during a period when measles outbreaks accounted for 87% of confirmed U.S. cases in 2025. The flags were designed to be highly visible and integrated with registry functionality to enable longitudinal tracking of suspected, confirmed, and exposed patients. Three distinct flags with specific criteria were created to assist facilities in case tracking, exposure management, and infection prevention. While the implementation represents a novel and scalable approach, the evidence provided is descriptive and does not evaluate the flags' impact on transmission reduction or clinical outcomes, limiting the strength of conclusions to feasibility and preparedness.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 2025 年,麻疹 暴发 导致了美国 87% 的确诊病例,这凸显了医疗机构需要快速扩展的准备措施。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究在 Mayo Clinic 机构进行,感染预防和控制 (IPAC) 与护理信息学合作,为疑似、确诊和暴露患者开发 麻疹 特定的电子健康记录 (EHR) 标记。
elements_zh.methods: EHR 标志设计得高度可见,并与登记功能集成,以实现对暴露病例和确诊病例的纵向跟踪,支持感染预防和控制调查以及临床操作。
elements_zh.main_results: EHR 中开发了三个不同的 麻疹 特定标志,每个标志都有表 1 中概述的具体使用标准。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将 EHR 标志解释为一种新颖且可实施的工具,可在 麻疹 暴发 期间协助设施进行病例跟踪、暴露管理以及感染预防和控制。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: EHR 中的 麻疹 标志可以通过改善医疗机构中的病例跟踪、暴露管理和实时响应能力来为感染预防策略提供信息。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 所提供的证据并未报告 EHR 标志在减少 麻疹 传播 或改善临床结果方面的有效性,从而将证据的强度限制为描述性实施研究。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 2025 年,麻疹 暴发 导致了美国 87% 的确诊病例,这凸显了医疗机构需要快速扩展的准备措施。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究在 Mayo Clinic 机构进行,感染预防和控制 (IPAC) 与护理信息学合作,为疑似、确诊和暴露患者开发 麻疹 特定的电子健康记录 (EHR) 标记。
analysis_zh.methods: EHR 标志设计得高度可见,并与登记功能集成,以实现对暴露病例和确诊病例的纵向跟踪,支持感染预防和控制调查以及临床操作。
analysis_zh.main_results: EHR 中开发了三个不同的 麻疹 特定标志,每个标志都有表 1 中概述的具体使用标准。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将 EHR 标志解释为一种新颖且可实施的工具,可在 麻疹 暴发 期间协助设施进行病例跟踪、暴露管理以及感染预防和控制。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: EHR 中的 麻疹 标志可以通过改善医疗机构中的病例跟踪、暴露管理和实时响应能力来为感染预防策略提供信息。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 所提供的证据并未报告 EHR 标志在减少 麻疹 传播 或改善临床结果方面的有效性,从而将证据的强度限制为描述性实施研究。

S1):s15–s16 doi:10.1017/ash.2026.10450 Presentation Type: Top Poster Abstract Subject Category: Occupational Health Abstract ID: 298 Genomic Epidemiology Demonstrates that Decolonization reduces Staphylococcus aureus transmission in a Neonatal Intensive Care Unit Kayla Ruch1 and Mayar Al Mohajer2 1Becton Dickinson (BD) and 2Baylor College of Medicine Background: Infection preventionists (IPs) increasingly lead systemwide healthcare epidemiology functions integrating infection prevention, anti- microbial stewardship, and preparedness for emerging pathogens. The Advanced Leadership Certification in Infection Prevention and Control (AL-CIP) is the first credential to formally assess advanced IPC leadership competencies, yet the leadership practices, epidemiologic decision-making, and risk management strategies employed by certified professionals have not been empirically described. Methods: The Leadership Evaluation and Development for Infection Preventionists (LEAD-IP) study used an obser- vational nested cohort design. Secondary portfolio data from AL-CIP applicants across two 2025 certification cycles were analyzed to character- ize demographic and professional attributes. A nested cohort of certified professionals (18%) completed a structured 60-minute qualitative inter- view via Microsoft Teams. Interviews followed the IRB-approved 34-item LEAD-IP instrument assessing leadership behaviors, healthcare epidemi- ology decision-making, antimicrobial stewardship engagement, risk assessment practices, communication strategies, and preparedness for emerging pathogens. Data were managed in REDCap and analyzed using Braun and Clarke’s inductive thematic analysis with a structured code- book, triangulation, and verification of thematic saturation. Results: Thirty AL-CIP–certified leaders across healthcare systems, public health agencies, and academic settings participated. Across seven themes, partic- ipants described a shift from task-based practice to systems-level health- care epidemiology leadership, integrating surveillance data, antimicrobial resistance patterns, and organizational risk indicators into strategic direction-setting. Leaders emphasized dashboards, analytic tools, and improvement models to detect outbreaks earlier, evaluate stewardship interventions, and guide resource allocation. Transparent communication and psychological safety facilitated early escalation of HAI clusters, anti- biotic misuse, environmental risks, and emerging pathogen concerns such as Candida auris. Participants reported persistent public health infrastruc- ture limitations, including fragmented reporting pathways, inconsistent data-sharing with health departments, and delays in organism identifica- tion that impeded timely epidemiologic response. Significant antibiotic stewardship gaps were also identified—particularly limited analytic capac- ity, insufficient infectious disease support, and low organizational priori- tization. Structural barriers such as staffing shortages and limited protected time constrained proactive IPC and stewardship leadership. Inclusive engagement of under-resourced teams improved situational awareness and intervention success. Proactive risk management—monitoring con- struction, airflow disruptions, MDRO trends, and public health alerts— was viewed as essential. AL-CIP certification strengthened leadership iden- tity, credibility, and strategic influence. Conclusions: AL-CIP–certified professionals demonstrated advanced capabilities in healthcare epidemiol- ogy, antibiotic stewardship, and public health preparedness through sys- tems thinking, data-driven decision-making, inclusive engagement, and proactive risk management. The AL-CIP credential enhanced leaders’ confidence and organizational impact, supporting a more resilient and pre- pared healthcare epidemiology workforce. analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to evaluate the impact of genomic epidemiology on reducing Staphylococcus aureus transmission in a Neonatal Intensive Care Unit, addressing the need for improved infection prevention strategies.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study used an observational nested cohort design, analyzing secondary portfolio data from AL-CIP applicants across two 2025 certification cycles, with a nested cohort of certified professionals (18%) completing structured interviews.
analysis.methods: Data were managed in REDCap and analyzed using Braun and Clarke’s inductive thematic analysis with a structured code-book, triangulation, and verification of thematic saturation.
analysis.main_results: Thirty AL-CIP–certified leaders across healthcare systems, public health agencies, and academic settings participated. Leaders emphasized dashboards, analytic tools, and improvement models to detect outbreaks earlier, evaluate stewardship interventions, and guide resource allocation.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that genomic epidemiology can enhance leadership practices in infection prevention by integrating surveillance data, antimicrobial resistance patterns, and organizational risk indicators into strategic decision-making.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results highlight the potential of genomic epidemiology to improve outbreak detection, stewardship interventions, and resource allocation, with implications for strengthening public health infrastructure and leadership in infectious disease control.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on self-reported data and the absence of direct transmission measurements, but the evidence is supported by structured interviews and thematic analysis, providing a moderate confidence assessment.

analysis.summary_en: This study explores the role of genomic epidemiology in reducing Staphylococcus aureus transmission within a Neonatal Intensive Care Unit. It evaluates the impact of the Advanced Leadership Certification in Infection Prevention and Control (AL-CIP) on leadership practices, emphasizing the shift from task-based to systems-level healthcare epidemiology. The study used an observational nested cohort design, analyzing data from AL-CIP applicants and conducting structured interviews with certified professionals. Results showed that leaders utilized dashboards and analytic tools to detect outbreaks earlier and guide resource allocation. The findings suggest that genomic epidemiology can enhance strategic decision-making by integrating surveillance data and resistance patterns. The study highlights the importance of leadership in infection prevention and identifies persistent public health infrastructure limitations. However, the reliance on self-reported data and lack of direct transmission measurements limit the confidence in the findings, resulting in a moderate assessment of evidence strength.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在评估基因组 流行病学 对减少新生儿重症监护病房中金黄色葡萄球菌 传播 的影响,满足改进感染预防策略的需求。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究采用观察性嵌套 队列研究 设计,分析 AL-CIP 申请人在两个 2025 年认证周期中的二级作品集数据,并由完成结构化面试的认证专业人士 (18%) 进行嵌套 队列研究。
elements_zh.methods: 数据在 REDCap 中进行管理,并使用 Braun 和 Clarke 的归纳主题分析以及结构化密码本、三角测量和主题饱和度验证进行分析。
elements_zh.main_results: 来自医疗保健系统、公共卫生机构和学术机构的 30 名 AL-CIP 认证领导者参加了此次活动。领导者强调仪表板、分析工具和改进模型,以更早地发现 暴发、评估管理干预措施并指导资源分配。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,基因组 流行病学 可以通过将 监测 数据、抗菌药物耐药模式和组织风险指标整合到战略决策中来增强感染预防方面的领导实践。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 结果凸显了基因组 流行病学 在改善 暴发 检测、管理干预和资源分配方面的潜力,对加强公共卫生基础设施和传染病控制领导力具有影响。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究由于依赖自我报告的数据且缺乏直接的 传播 测量而受到限制,但证据得到结构化访谈和主题分析的支持,提供了适度的置信度评估。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在评估基因组 流行病学 对减少新生儿重症监护病房中金黄色葡萄球菌 传播 的影响,满足改进感染预防策略的需求。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究采用观察性嵌套 队列研究 设计,分析 AL-CIP 申请人在两个 2025 年认证周期中的二级作品集数据,并由完成结构化面试的认证专业人士 (18%) 进行嵌套 队列研究。
analysis_zh.methods: 数据在 REDCap 中进行管理,并使用 Braun 和 Clarke 的归纳主题分析以及结构化密码本、三角测量和主题饱和度验证进行分析。
analysis_zh.main_results: 来自医疗保健系统、公共卫生机构和学术机构的 30 名 AL-CIP 认证领导者参加了此次活动。领导者强调仪表板、分析工具和改进模型,以更早地发现 暴发、评估管理干预措施并指导资源分配。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,基因组 流行病学 可以通过将 监测 数据、抗菌药物耐药模式和组织风险指标整合到战略决策中来增强感染预防方面的领导实践。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 结果凸显了基因组 流行病学 在改善 暴发 检测、管理干预和资源分配方面的潜力,对加强公共卫生基础设施和传染病控制领导力具有影响。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究由于依赖自我报告的数据且缺乏直接的 传播 测量而受到限制,但证据得到结构化访谈和主题分析的支持,提供了适度的置信度评估。

S1):s188–s189 doi:10.1017/ash.2026.10734 Presentation Type: Poster Presentation Subject Category: Technology Abstract ID: 284 How Clean is Clean? Mitigation Efforts of Ice/water Dispensers Linked to a Mycobacterium chelonae Outbreak at a Pediatric Hospital Alyssa Olson1, Jean Barth1, Jenna Rasmusson1, Nicole Kriewall1, Cory Kudrna, Todd Sheley, Tyler Kramer, Jason Buckmeier and John OHoro2 1Mayo Clinic and 2Mayo Clinic College of Medicine Background: We had a large-scale measles exposure event affecting 626 patients. Management of exposed patients was urgent, involving quaran- tine, post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP), and symptom monitoring on a case-by-case basis. Cases were initially tracked and managed using a com- bination of multiple spreadsheets amongst stakeholders as well as lists within the electronic health record (EHR). Using shared spreadsheets and lists created significant challenges with maintaining and editing multi- ple copies and updating workbooks simultaneously. Methods: Infection Prevention and Control (IPAC) worked with primary care personnel and EHR developers to create a shared registry that would prioritize com- munication and follow-up for exposed patients based on age and immun- ity. Patients are initially added to the shared registry within the EHR by reviewing non-registry reports and tagging patients, identified using expo- sure timeframes that overlapped with the index measles cases, in a manner that transferred them to the shared registry. From this registry, measles, mumps, and rubella vaccine status can be confirmed, immune status can be identified, and criteria for PEP assigned. High-risk patients are then contacted with recommendations from IPAC and primary care. Communication and follow-up are tracked directly within the shared regis- try to ensure appropriate patient management. The exposure management registry is further leveraged throughout the measles outbreak timeframe by allowing real-time monitoring of patients that require additional precau- tions or guidance related to their exposure. Result: The shared registry enhanced documentation accuracy and transparency between stakehold- ers. It led to availability of real-time status of exposed patients for the dura- tion of the measles outbreak timeframe. Overall, the registry enabled time- sensitive patient communication to all exposed patients and rapid identi- fication of those who needed PEP. Communication could happen rapidly and seamlessly between care teams within the organization, and the nec- essary information could be shared quickly with public health authorities as required. Conclusion: Large scale exposures are a challenge to manage and ensure appropriate action and communication occurs. Errors can be prevented by having a single shared exposure management registry. A registry enables care teams to quickly identify and prioritize patients for measles follow-up, communication, PEP, and ongoing management across outbreak timeframes. This process reduces both time and operational bur- dens of exposure follow-up tracking outside of the EHR. Antimicrobial Stewardship & Healthcare Epidemiology 2026;6(Suppl. S1):s189 doi:10.1017/ash.2026.10735 Presentation Type: Poster Presentation Subject Category: Technology Abstract ID: 315 Connecting the Patients: Network Analysis of a Multi-facility Candidozyma auris Outbreak, Georgia, September 2024 – August 2025 Erin Marshall1, Michael Sayer, Christian Schneider2, Lacey Bergerhofer1 and Azadeh Wickam 1Children's Mercy and 2Children's Mercy Kansas City Background: Central line-associated bloodstream infection (CLABSI) rep- resents the most common and costly device-associated hospital-acquired infection in children. While prevention bundles are effective when reliably implemented, pediatric-specific risks often require strategies beyond stan- dard bundles. Existing CLABSI risk models are insufficient for pediatric patients, remaining static during their hospital stay despite changing clini- cal conditions. Moreover, previously reported dashboards and predictive models generally do not incorporate data science principles to provide a daily prediction score, and they often exclude demographic factors beyond age and sex. The purpose of developing the CLABSI risk model was to lev- erage technology-driven strategies for identifying, intervening, and escalat- ing care for high-risk pediatric patients in real time, thereby decreasing infection risk. Methods: Quality Improvement, Data Intelligence, and the interdisciplinary clinical team partnered to develop an evidence-based predictive model tailored to institutional risk factors. Using evidence and clinical expertise, an affinity diagram was created. Data from 61,068 in- patient central line days (January 2022- July 2024), sourced from electronic health records (EHR) and clinical surveillance software, formed the data- set. CLABSI was identified using NHSN surveillance definition. Patient risk factors from the infection date plus two days prior were evaluated. Exploratory data analysis was completed using RStudio integrated devel- opment environment to inform model development. Separate models were created for nontunneled lines and tunneled lines. Prediction models were developed using Python coding language and Databricks data intelligence platform. Under-sampling was used to account for uneven distribution between CLABSI and non-CLABSI cases. Logistic regression, random for- est, and XGBoost models were created. Candidate models were compared using area under the curve (AUC), sensitivity, and specificity. Result: Using the XGBoost model for nontunneled line, the test AUC was 0.831, demonstrating strong discriminative power. This model achieved a sensitivity of 0.828, indicating its ability to correctly identify a high pro- portion of actual CLABSI cases, and a specificity of 0.751, reflecting its capacity to correctly identify non-CLABSI cases. Similarly, the tunneled line XGBoost model yielded an AUC of 0.845, showcasing excellent pre- dictive performance. Its sensitivity was 0.833 and specificity was 0.668. In both models, the number of modifiable risks was the most significant factor (Tables 1-3). Conclusion: The CLABSI prediction model enables real-time identification and intervention to support proactive prevention, SHEA Spring 2026 Abstracts 2026;6 Suppl 1 S189

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addressed the challenge of managing large-scale measles exposures in a pediatric hospital where rapid identification and follow-up of exposed patients were needed to prevent errors and ensure appropriate post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP).
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study described the implementation of a shared exposure management registry within an electronic health record (EHR) system at a pediatric hospital to track and manage patients exposed to measles during a large-scale outbreak affecting 626 patients.
analysis.methods: The registry was created by Infection Prevention and Control (IPAC) in collaboration with primary care personnel and EHR developers to prioritize communication and follow-up for exposed patients based on age and immunity. Patients were added to the registry by reviewing non-registry reports and tagging those within overlapping exposure timeframes, enabling confirmation of vaccine status, immune status identification, and assignment of PEP criteria.
analysis.main_results: The shared registry enhanced documentation accuracy and transparency between stakeholders, provided real-time status of exposed patients throughout the outbreak, and enabled time-sensitive patient communication and rapid identification of those needing PEP.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors concluded that large-scale exposures are difficult to manage and that errors can be prevented by using a single shared exposure management registry, which reduces operational burdens and improves efficiency in outbreak response.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The registry facilitates real-time monitoring, prioritization, and management of exposed patients, supporting timely communication and PEP administration during measles outbreaks in pediatric settings.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is limited to a single-center, retrospective implementation without comparative data to standard practices, which may affect generalizability and strength of conclusions.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the use of a shared exposure management registry within an electronic health record system to manage a large-scale measles outbreak affecting 626 pediatric patients. The registry was developed collaboratively by Infection Prevention and Control, primary care personnel, and EHR developers to prioritize follow-up based on age and immunity. Patients were added to the registry by tagging those within overlapping exposure timeframes, enabling confirmation of vaccine status, immune status identification, and assignment of post-exposure prophylaxis criteria. The registry improved documentation accuracy, transparency, and real-time monitoring of exposed patients, facilitating timely communication and rapid identification of those needing prophylaxis. The authors concluded that a single shared registry prevents errors and reduces operational burdens during large-scale exposures, though the evidence is limited to a single-center, retrospective implementation without comparative data.

analysis_en.research_question_and_background: The study addressed the challenge of managing large-scale measles exposures in a pediatric hospital where rapid identification and follow-up of exposed patients were needed to prevent errors and ensure appropriate post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP).
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: The study described the implementation of a shared exposure management registry within an electronic health record (EHR) system at a pediatric hospital to track and manage patients exposed to measles during a large-scale outbreak affecting 626 patients.
analysis_en.methods: The registry was created by Infection Prevention and Control (IPAC) in collaboration with primary care personnel and EHR developers to prioritize communication and follow-up for exposed patients based on age and immunity. analysis_en.main_results: The shared registry enhanced documentation accuracy and transparency between stakeholders, provided real-time status of exposed patients throughout the outbreak, and enabled time-sensitive patient communication and rapid identification of those needing PEP.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors concluded that large-scale exposures are difficult to manage and that errors can be prevented by using a single shared exposure management registry, which reduces operational burdens and improves efficiency in outbreak response.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The registry facilitates real-time monitoring, prioritization, and management of exposed patients, supporting timely communication and PEP administration during measles outbreaks in pediatric settings.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is limited to a single-center, retrospective implementation without comparative data to standard practices, which may affect generalizability and strength of conclusions.
